915.g: ਕਾ ਸੌ ਕਹੌ ਸੰਗ ਕੋਊ ਨਾਹੀ ॥
915.t: kaa sau kahau sa(n)g kouoo naahee ||

915.g: ਇਹ ਚਿੰਤਾ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਮਨ ਮਾਹੀ ॥੧੬॥
915.t: eeh chi(n)taa taa ke man maahee ||16||
915.e: ‘I have no one to help me,’ that apprehension captured his mind.(16)
Dohira

915.g: ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਘੋਰਾ ਨਹੀ ਸਾਥੀ ਸੰਗ ਨ ਕੋਇ ॥
915.t: sasatr asatr ghoraa nahee saathee sa(n)g na koi ||
915.e: ‘Neither I have arms, nor I possess any horses. I have no companion.

915.g: ਅਤਿ ਮੁਸਕਿਲ ਮੋ ਕੌ ਬਨੀ ਕਰਤਾ ਕਰੈ ਸੁ ਹੋਇ ॥੧੭॥
915.t: at musakil mo kau banee karataa karai su hoi ||17||
915.e: ‘I am plunged in a great predicament. Now, only God can help me.(17)

915.g: ਸਾਥੀ ਕੋਊ ਸੰਗ ਨਹੀ ਕਾ ਸੋ ਕਰੋ ਪੁਕਾਰ ॥
915.t: saathee kouoo sa(n)g nahee kaa so karo pukaar ||
915.e: ‘I have no friend, who could cry for help?

915.g: ਮਨਸਾ ਬਾਚਾ ਕਰਮਨਾ ਮੋਹਿ ਹਨਿ ਹੈ ਨਿਰਧਾਰ ॥੧੮॥
915.t: manasaa baachaa karamanaa moh han hai niradhaar ||18||
915.e: ‘To prove her words, she must have ascertained to terminate me.’(18)

915.g: ਖਾਇ ਮਿਠਾਈ ਰਾਵ ਤਬ ਦੀਯੋ ਪਿਟਾਰੋ ਦਾਨ ॥
915.t: khai miThaiee raav tab dheeyo piTaaro dhaan ||
915.e: The Raja savoured some sweetment and, then, bestowed the rest of the basket with benediction.

915.g: ਵਹ ਬਿਵਾਹਿ ਤਿਹ ਲੈ ਗਯੋ ਅਧਿਕ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਸੁਖੁ ਮਾਨਿ ॥੧੯॥
915.t: veh bivaeh teh lai gayo adhik hiradhai sukh maan ||19||
915.e: Thereafter, he married her and with great satisfaction took her with him.(l9)

915.g: ਦੁਹਿਤ ਜਾਮਾਤਾ ਸਹਿਤ ਜੀਯਤ ਦਯੋ ਪਠਾਇ ॥
915.t: dhuhit jaamaataa sahit jeeyat dhayo paThai ||
915.e: The woman bade goodbye to her daughter along with the son-in-law,

915.g: ਸਭ ਦੇਖਤ ਦਿਨ ਕਾਢਿਯੋ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਹਿ ਮਠਾਈ ਖ੍ਵਾਇ ॥੨੦॥
915.t: sabh dhekhat dhin kaaddiyo nirapeh maThaiee khavaiai ||20||
915.e: And she accomplished this just by making Raja to eat some sweetments.(20)
Chaupaee
No body, not even the gods and the demons, can grasp the Chritars.

915.g: ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਸਮਝਿ ਮੋਨਿ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਰਹਿਯੋ ॥੨੧॥
915.t: chit mai samajh mon havai rahiyo ||21||
915.e: What should we designate and Chritar? It is rather prudent to keep quiet. (21)(1)

920.e: He played the flute; all the women were captivated.(6)
Dohira

920.g: ਸਭ ਅਬਲਾ ਮੋਹਿਤ ਭਈ ਨਾਦ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਪਾਇ ॥
920.t: sabh abalaa mohit bhiee naadh sravan sun pai ||
920.e: As soon as the music overwhelmed, the women were entranced,

920.g: ਸਭਹਿਨ ਕੇ ਤਨ ਸੌ ਗਏ ਕਮਲ ਪਤ੍ਰ ਲਪਟਾਇ ॥੭॥
920.t: sabhahin ke tan sau ge kamal patr lapaTai ||7||
920.e: And the leaves of lotus flowers stuck to their bodies.(7)
Chaupaee
Raja immediately slipped Madhwan Nal out and,

920.g: ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਜਾਨਿ ਜਿਯ ਤੇ ਨਹੀ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
920.t: bipr jaan jiy te nahee maariyo ||
920.e: Being of Brahmin caste, did not let him die.
He (Brahmin) walked away and came to Kamwati, the town of Cupid,
There he was fancied by the Kaamkandla (Cupid’s female counterpart).(8)
Dohira

920.g: ਕਾਮ ਸੈਨ ਰਾਜਾ ਜਹਾ ਤਹ ਦਿਜ ਪਹੂੰਚ੍ਯੋ ਜਾਇ ॥
920.t: kaam sain raajaa jahaa teh dhij pahoo(n)chayo jai ||
920.e: The Brahmin reached the place, of which, Kam (literally Cupid) Sen Was the Raja,

920.g: ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਤੀਨਿ ਸੈ ਸਾਠਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਨਾਚਤ ਜਹਾ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੯॥
920.t: pragaT teen sai saaTh tiray naachat jahaa banai ||9||
920.e: In whose court three hundred and sixty damsels used to dance.(9)
Chaupaee
Madhwan reached the court and bowed his head in obeisance.
A number of valiant ones were present there and Kaamkandla was dancing.(10)
Dohira

920.g: ਚੰਦਨ ਕੀ ਤਨ ਕੰਚੁਕੀ ਕਾਮਾ ਕਸੀ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
920.t: cha(n)dhan kee tan ka(n)chukee kaamaa kasee banai ||
920.e: Very tightly, Kama (Kaamkandla) had worn a sandalwood-scented bodice,

920.g: ਅੰਗਿਯਾ ਹੀ ਸਭ ਕੋ ਲਖੈ ਚੰਦਨ ਲਖ੍ਯੋ ਨ ਜਾਇ ॥੧੧॥
920.t: a(n)giyaa hee sabh ko lakhai cha(n)dhan lakhayo na jai ||11||
920.e: The bodice was visible but not the sandalwood.(11)

920.g: ਚੰਦਨ ਕੀ ਲੈ ਬਾਸਨਾ ਭਵਰ ਬਹਿਠ੍ਯੋ ਆਇ ॥
920.t: cha(n)dhan kee lai baasanaa bhavar bahiThayo aai ||
920.e: Lured by the aroma of sandalwood, a black-bee came and sat over it.

920.g: ਸੋ ਤਿਨ ਕੁਚ ਕੀ ਬਾਯੁ ਤੇ ਦੀਨੌ ਤਾਹਿ ਉਠਾਇ ॥੧੨॥
920.t: so tin kuch kee baay te dheenau taeh uThai ||12||
920.e: She jerked her bodice and made the bee fly away.(l2)
Chaupaee

920.g: ਇਹ ਸੁ ਭੇਦ ਬਿਪ ਨੈ ਲਹਿ ਲਯੋ ॥
920.t: eeh su bhedh bip nai leh layo ||

920.e: Brahmin observed all the interlude and felt very desirous,

920.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਦਰਬੁ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਤੇ ਜੋ ਲੀਨੋ ॥
920.t: amit dharab nirap te jo leeno ||

920.e: And all the wealth he was rewarded by Raja, he gave away to Kaamkandla.(13)
Dohira

920.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਦਰਬੁ ਹਮ ਜੋ ਦਯੋ ਸੋ ਇਹ ਦਯੋ ਲੁਟਾਇ ॥
920.t: amit dharab ham jo dhayo so ieh dhayo luTai ||
920.e: (The Raja thought) ‘All the wealth which I handed over to him, he has given away.

920.g: ਐਸੇ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਫਜੂਲ ਕੋ ਮੋਹਿ ਨ ਰਾਖ੍ਯੋ ਜਾਇ ॥੧੪॥
920.t: aaise bipr fajool ko moh na raakhayo jai ||14||
920.e: ‘Such a foolish Brahmin priest could not be retained by me.’(l4)
Chaupaee

920.g: ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਜਾਨਿ ਜਿਯ ਤੇ ਨਹਿ ਮਰਿਯੈ ॥
920.t: bipr jaan jiy te neh mariyai ||

920.g: ਇਹ ਪੁਰ ਤੇ ਇਹ ਤੁਰਤੁ ਨਿਕਰਿਯੈ ॥
920.t: eeh pur te ieh turat nikariyai ||
920.e: ‘Being a Brahmin he should not be killed but he must be banished from the village,

920.g: ਜਾ ਕੇ ਦੁਰਿਯੋ ਧਾਮ ਲਹਿ ਲੀਜੈ ॥
920.t: jaa ke dhuriyo dhaam leh leejai ||

920.e: ‘And any person who shelters him, he would be cut into pieces.’(15)

920.g: ਯਹ ਸਭ ਭੇਦ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਸੁਨਿ ਪਾਯੋ ॥
920.t: yeh sabh bhedh bipr sun paayo ||

920.e: When Brahmin learned about this secret proclamation, he instantly came to the house of that woman,

920.g: ਮੋ ਪਰ ਕੋਪ ਅਧਿਕ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਕੀਨੋ ॥
920.t: mo par kop adhik nirap keeno ||

920.e: (And said) ‘As the Raja is very angry with me, therefore, I have come to your house.’(16)
Dohira

921.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਬਚਨ ਕਾਮਾ ਤੁਰਤ ਦਿਜ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਲਯੋ ਦੁਰਾਇ ॥
921.t: sunat bachan kaamaa turat dhij gireh layo dhurai ||
921.e: Listening to this, Kama hid him in her house,

921.g: ਰਾਜਾ ਕੀ ਨਿੰਦ੍ਯਾ ਕਰੀ ਤਾਹਿ ਗਰੇ ਸੋ ਲਾਇ ॥੧੭॥
921.t: raajaa kee ni(n)dhayaa karee taeh gare so lai ||17||
921.e: And she flew into a rage and criticised Raja.(17)

921.g: ਕਾਮਾ ਬਾਚ ॥
921.t: kaamaa baach ||

921.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
921.t: chauapiee ||
921.e: Chaupaee

921.g: ਧ੍ਰਿਗ ਇਹ ਰਾਇ ਭੇਦ ਨਹਿ ਜਾਨਤ ॥
921.t: dhirag ieh rai bhedh neh jaanat ||
921.e: (She pronounced) ‘Curse be to Raja who did not grasp the secret.

921.g: ਤੁਮ ਸੇ ਚਤੁਰਨ ਸੌ ਰਿਸਿ ਠਾਨਤ ॥
921.t: tum se chaturan sau ris Thaanat ||
921.e: Became jealous of wise ones like you.

921.g: ਮਹਾ ਮੂੜ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਕੋ ਕਾ ਕਹਿਯੈ ॥
921.t: mahaa mooR nirap ko kaa kahiyai ||
921.e: ‘What can we say about such a blockhead.

921.g: ਯਾ ਪਾਪੀ ਕੇ ਦੇਸ ਨ ਰਹਿਯੈ ॥੧੮॥
921.t: yaa paapee ke dhes na rahiyai ||18||
921.e: One should not live in the country of such a vice-man.(l8)

921.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
921.t: dhoharaa ||
921.e: Dohira

921.g: ਚਲੌ ਤ ਏਕੈ ਮਗੁ ਚਲੌ ਰਹੇ ਰਹੌ ਤਿਹ ਗਾਉ ॥
921.t: chalau ta ekai mag chalau rahe rahau teh gaau ||
921.e: ‘Corne, let us take the same path and live side by side,

921.g: ਨਿਸੁ ਦਿਨ ਰਟੌ ਬਿਹੰਗ ਜ੍ਯੋ ਮੀਤ ਤਿਹਾਰੋ ਨਾਉ ॥੧੯॥
921.t: nis dhin raTau biha(n)g jayo meet tihaaro naau ||19||
921.e: ‘And I will always remember you and remain with you.’(19)

921.g: ਬਿਰਹ ਬਾਨ ਮੋ ਤਨ ਗਡੇ ਕਾ ਸੋ ਕਰੋ ਪੁਕਾਰ ॥
921.t: bireh baan mo tan gadde kaa so karo pukaar ||
921.e: ‘I have been pierced with the arrow of separation, how could I remonstrate?

921.g: ਤਨਕ ਅਗਨਿ ਕੋ ਸਿਵ ਭਏ ਜਰੌ ਸੰਭਾਰਿ ਸੰਭਾਰਿ ॥੨੦॥
921.t: tanak agan ko siv bhe jarau sa(n)bhaar sa(n)bhaar ||20||
921.e: ‘Slowly and steadily, I am scorching in the fire ofthis estrangement.(20)

921.g: ਆਜੁ ਸਖੀ ਮੈ ਯੌ ਸੁਨ੍ਯੋ ਪਹੁ ਫਾਟਤ ਪਿਯ ਗੌਨ ॥
921.t: aaj sakhee mai yau sunayo pahu faaTat piy gauan ||
921.e: ‘Oh, rny friends, I have heard that at the day break my lover will go away.

921.g: ਪਹੁ ਹਿਯਰੇ ਝਗਰਾ ਪਰਿਯੋ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਫਟਿ ਹੈ ਕੌਨ ॥੨੧॥
921.t: pahu hiyare jhagaraa pariyo pahile faT hai kauan ||21||
921.e: ‘The point is who will enact first (his leaving and rising of Sun).(21)

921.g: ਮਾਧਵ ਬਾਚ ॥
921.t: maadhav baach ||
921.e: Madhwan Talk

921.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
921.t: chauapiee ||
921.e: Chaupaee

921.g: ਤੁਮ ਸੁਖ ਸੋ ਸੁੰਦਰਿ ਹ੍ਯਾਂ ਰਹੋ ॥
921.t: tum sukh so su(n)dhar hayaa(n) raho ||

921.g: ਹਮ ਕੋ ਬੇਗਿ ਬਿਦਾ ਮੁਖ ਕਹੋ ॥
921.t: ham ko beg bidhaa mukh kaho ||
921.e: ‘You, the pretty one, stay here in bliss and bid me good-bye.

921.g: ਹਮਰੋ ਕਛੂ ਤਾਪ ਨਹ ਕਰਿਯਹੁ ॥
921.t: hamaro kachhoo taap neh kariyahu ||

921.g: ਨਿਤ ਰਾਮ ਕੋ ਨਾਮ ਸੰਭਰਿਯਹੁ ॥੨੨॥
921.t: nit raam ko naam sa(n)bhariyahu ||22||
921.e: ‘Do not be alarmed about me and meditate on god Rama’s name.’(22)

921.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
921.t: dhoharaa ||
921.e: Dohira

921.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਬਚਨ ਕਾਮਾ ਤਬੈ ਭੂਮਿ ਪਰੀ ਮੁਰਛਾਇ ॥
921.t: sunat bachan kaamaa tabai bhoom paree murachhai ||
921.e: Hearing the advice, the lady became unconscious and fell flat on the ground,

921.g: ਜਨੁ ਘਾਯਲ ਘਾਇਨ ਲਗੇ ਗਿਰੈ ਉਠੈ ਬਰਰਾਇ ॥੨੩॥
921.t: jan ghaayal ghain lage girai uThai bararai ||23||
921.e: Like the injured man, tried to get up but fell down again.(23)

921.g: ਸੋਰਠਾ ॥
921.t: soraThaa ||
921.e: Sortha

921.g: ਅਧਿਕ ਬਿਰਹ ਕੇ ਸੰਗ ਪੀਤ ਬਰਨ ਕਾਮਾ ਭਈ ॥
921.t: adhik bireh ke sa(n)g peet baran kaamaa bhiee ||
921.e: In the wake of separation, Kama looked anaemic.

921.g: ਰਕਤ ਨ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਅੰਗ ਚਲਿਯੋ ਮੀਤ ਚੁਰਾਇ ਚਿਤ ॥੨੪॥
921.t: rakat na rahiyo a(n)g chaliyo meet churai chit ||24||
921.e: As the paramour had gone after stealing her heart; she looked totally drained.(24)

921.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
921.t: dhoharaa ||

921.g: ਟਾਕ ਤੋਲ ਤਨ ਨ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਮਾਸਾ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਨ ਮਾਸ ॥
921.t: Taak tol tan na rahiyo maasaa rahiyo na maas ||

921.g: ਬਿਰਹਿਨ ਕੌ ਤੀਨੋ ਭਲੇ ਹਾਡ ਚਾਮ ਅਰੁ ਸ੍ਵਾਸ ॥੨੫॥
921.t: birahin kau teeno bhale haadd chaam ar savaiaas ||25||

921.g: ਅਤਿ ਕਾਮਾ ਲੋਟਤ ਧਰਨਿ ਮਾਧਵਨਲ ਕੇ ਹੇਤ ॥
921.t: at kaamaa loTat dharan maadhavanal ke het ||
921.e: The separation of Madhwan made her to roll over on the ground,

921.g: ਟੂਟੋ ਅਮਲ ਅਫੀਮਿਯਹਿ ਜਨੁ ਪਸਵਾਰੇ ਲੇਤ ॥੨੬॥
921.t: TooTo amal afeemiyeh jan pasavaare let ||26||
921.e: Like an addict of opium, she tossed around in the dust.(26)

921.g: ਮਿਲਤ ਨੈਨ ਨਹਿ ਰਹਿ ਸਕਤ ਜਾਨਤ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਪਤੰਗ ॥
921.t: milat nain neh reh sakat jaanat preet pata(n)g ||

921.g: ਛੂਟਤ ਬਿਰਹ ਬਿਯੋਗ ਤੇ ਹੋਮਤ ਅਪਨੋ ਅੰਗ ॥੨੭॥
921.t: chhooTat bireh biyog te homat apano a(n)g ||27||

921.g: ਕਾਮਾ ਬਾਚ ॥
921.t: kaamaa baach ||
921.e: Kama Talk

921.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
921.t: chauapiee ||
921.e: Chaupaee

921.g: ਖੰਡ ਖੰਡ ਕੈ ਤੀਰਥ ਕਰਿਹੌ ॥
921.t: kha(n)dd kha(n)dd kai teerath karihau ||

921.g: ਬਾਰਿ ਅਨੇਕ ਆਗਿ ਮੈ ਬਰਿਹੌ ॥
921.t: baar anek aag mai barihau ||
921.e: ‘I will go around the pilgrim places and, again and again, will burn in fire of alienation.

921.g: ਕਾਸੀ ਬਿਖੈ ਕਰਵਤਿਹਿ ਪੈਹੌ ॥
921.t: kaasee bikhai karavateh paihau ||

921.g: ਢੂੰਢਿ ਮੀਤ ਤੋ ਕੌ ਤਊ ਲੈਹੌ ॥੨੮॥
921.t: ddoo(n)dd meet to kau tuoo laihau ||28||
921.e: ‘I will face the saw at Kanshi but will never rest till I find you.(28)

921.g: ਅੜਿਲ ॥
921.t: aRil ||
921.e: Arril

921.g: ਜਹਾ ਪਿਯਰਵਾ ਚਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਤਿਤਹੀ ਚਲੇ ॥
921.t: jahaa piyaravaa chale praan titahee chale ||
921.e: ‘Where there is love, there is my life.

921.g: ਸਕਲ ਸਿਥਿਲ ਭਏ ਅੰਗ ਸੰਗ ਜੈ ਹੈ ਭਲੇ ॥
921.t: sakal sithil bhe a(n)g sa(n)g jai hai bhale ||
921.e: ‘All my body limbs are getting exhausted.

921.g: ਮਾਧਵਨਲ ਕੌ ਨਾਮੁ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਸੋ ਜਾਨਿਯੈ ॥
921.t: maadhavanal kau naam ma(n)tr so jaaniyai ||
921.e: ‘I need the charm of Madhwan,

921.g: ਹੋ ਜਾਤੌ ਲਗਤ ਉਚਾਟ ਸਤਿ ਕਰਿ ਮਾਨਿਯੈ ॥੨੯॥
921.t: ho jaatau lagat uchaaT sat kar maaniyai ||29||
921.e: ‘As my heart is yearning without him.’(29)

921.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
921.t: dhoharaa ||
921.e: Dohira

921.g: ਜੋ ਤੁਮਰੀ ਬਾਛਾ ਕਰਤ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਹਰੈ ਜਮ ਮੋਹਿ ॥
921.t: jo tumaree baachhaa karat praan harai jam moh ||
921.e: ‘If the god of death takes out my life in your remembrance,

921.g: ਮਰੇ ਪਰਾਤ ਚੁਰੈਲ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਚਮਕਿ ਚਿਤੈਹੌ ਤੋਹਿ ॥੩੦॥
921.t: mare paraat churail havai chamak chitaihau toh ||30||
921.e: ‘I will become witch and keep on roaming and searching for you.(30)

921.g: ਬਰੀ ਬਿਰਹ ਕੀ ਆਗਿ ਮੈ ਜਰੀ ਰਖੈ ਹੌ ਨਾਉ ॥
921.t: baree bireh kee aag mai jaree rakhai hau naau ||
921.e: ‘Burning in the fire of passion,

921.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਜਰੀ ਕੀ ਬਰੀ ਕੀ ਢਿਗ ਤੇ ਕਬਹੂੰ ਨ ਜਾਉ ॥੩੧॥
921.t: bhaat jaree kee baree kee ddig te kabahoo(n) na jaau ||31||
921.e: I will adopt my name as “the burnt one”.(31)

921.g: ਸਾਚ ਕਹਤ ਹੈ ਬਿਰਹਨੀ ਰਹੀ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਸੌ ਪਾਗਿ ॥
921.t: saach kahat hai birahanee rahee prem sau paag ||
921.e: ‘I say truthfully that a disengaged one burns in love,

921.g: ਡਰਤ ਬਿਰਹ ਕੀ ਅਗਨਿ ਸੌ ਜਰਤ ਕਾਠ ਕੀ ਆਗਿ ॥੩੨॥
921.t: ddarat bireh kee agan sau jarat kaaTh kee aag ||32||
921.e: ‘Exactly like the dry wood blazes with crackling sounds.’(32)

921.g: ਤਬ ਮਾਧਵਨਲ ਉਠਿ ਚਲਿਯੋ ਭਯੋ ਪਵਨ ਕੋ ਭੇਸ ॥
921.t: tab maadhavanal uTh chaliyo bhayo pavan ko bhes ||
921.e: In the meantime, Madhwan had flown away like air,

921.g: ਜਸ ਧੁਨਿ ਸੁਨਿ ਸਿਰ ਧੁਨਿ ਗਯੋ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਜਹਾ ਨਰੇਸ ॥੩੩॥
921.t: jas dhun sun sir dhun gayo bikram jahaa nares ||33||
921.e: And reached there where the reverend Bikrimajeet used to sit.(33)

921.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
921.t: chauapiee ||
921.e: Chaupaee

921.g: ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਜਹਾ ਨਿਤਿ ਚਲਿ ਆਵੈ ॥
921.t: bikram jahaa nit chal aavai ||

921.g: ਪੂਜਿ ਗੌਰਜਾ ਕੌ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਜਾਵੈ ॥
921.t: pooj gauarajaa kau gireh jaavai ||
921.e: Bikrim used to visit the place and perform prayers to goddess gory.

921.g: ਮੰਦਿਰ ਊਚ ਧੁਜਾ ਫਹਰਾਹੀ ॥
921.t: ma(n)dhir uooch dhujaa faharaahee ||

921.g: ਫਟਕਾਚਲ ਲਖਿ ਤਾਹਿ ਲਜਾਹੀ ॥੩੪॥
921.t: faTakaachal lakh taeh lajaahee ||34||
921.e: The temple was lofty and its grace was unsurpassable.(34)

921.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
921.t: dhoharaa ||
921.e: Dohira

921.g: ਤਿਹੀ ਠੌਰਿ ਮਾਧਵ ਗਯੋ ਦੋਹਾ ਲਿਖ੍ਯੋ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
921.t: tihee Thauar maadhav gayo dhohaa likhayo banai ||
921.e: Madhwan went there and wrote a couplet at the place,

921.g: ਜੌ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਇਹ ਬਾਚਿ ਹੈ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਹੋ ਮੋਰ ਉਪਾਇ ॥੩੫॥
921.t: jau bikram ieh baach hai havai ho mor upai ||35||
921.e: (Thinking) ‘When Bikrim reads it he will suggest some resolve for me.‘(35)

921.g: ਜੇ ਨਰ ਰੋਗਨ ਸੌ ਗ੍ਰਸੇ ਤਿਨ ਕੋ ਹੋਤ ਉਪਾਉ ॥
921.t: je nar rogan sau grase tin ko hot upaau ||
921.e: If a person is sick he can be suggested some remedy,

921.g: ਬਿਰਹ ਤ੍ਰਿਦੋਖਨ ਜੇ ਗ੍ਰਸੇ ਤਿਨ ਕੋ ਕਛੁ ਨ ਬਚਾਉ ॥੩੬॥
921.t: bireh tiradhokhan je grase tin ko kachh na bachaau ||36||
921.e: But for a person who is suffering from love-sickness, there is no sanctuary.(36)

921.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
921.t: chauapiee ||
921.e: Chaupaee

921.g: ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਸੈਨਿ ਤਹਾ ਚਲਿ ਆਯੋ ॥
921.t: bikram sain tahaa chal aayo ||

921.g: ਆਨ ਗੌਰਜਾ ਕੌ ਸਿਰ ਨ੍ਯਾਯੋ ॥
921.t: aan gauarajaa kau sir nayaayo ||
921.e: Bikrim came there in the evening and paid his obeisance to the goddess Gory,

921.g: ਬਾਚਿ ਦੋਹਰਾ ਕੋ ਚਕਿ ਰਹਿਯੋ ॥
921.t: baach dhoharaa ko chak rahiyo ||

921.g: ਕੋ ਬਿਰਹੀ ਆਯੋ ਹ੍ਯਾਂ ਕਹਿਯੋ ॥੩੭॥
921.t: ko birahee aayo hayaa(n) kahiyo ||37||
921.e: He read the couplet and inquired if there had come some love-sick person.(37)

921.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
921.t: dhoharaa ||
921.e: Dohira

921.g: ਕੋ ਬਿਰਹੀ ਆਯੋ ਹ੍ਯਾਂ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਲੇਹੁ ਬੁਲਾਇ ॥
921.t: ko birahee aayo hayaa(n) taa kau leh bulai ||
921.e: (She pronounced) ‘The one who is love-sick, has come here, call

921.g: ਜੋ ਵਹੁ ਕਹੈ ਸੋ ਹੌ ਕਰੌ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਜਿਯਨ ਉਪਾਇ ॥੩੮॥
921.t: jo vahu kahai so hau karau taa kau jiyan upai ||38||
921.e: Him. ‘Whatever he desires, I will fulfi1.’(38)

922.e: Chaupaee
Bikrim called Madhwan and asked him respectfully to be seated.
(Madhwan said) ‘Whatever the Brahmin priest orders,
I will abide by, even I may have to fight,’(39)
When Madhwan told the whole story,
Bikrim called all his army.
Arming themselves and putting the armour
They commenced march to the direction of Kamwati.(40)
Sortha

922.g: ਦੂਤ ਪਠਾਯੋ ਏਕ ਕਾਮਸੈਨ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਸੌ ਕਹੈ ॥
922.t: dhoot paThaayo ek kaamasain nirap sau kahai ||
922.e: He sent his emissary to (Raja) Kam Sen to give him the message,

922.g: ਕਾਮਕੰਦਲਾ ਏਕ ਦੈ ਸਭ ਦੇਸ ਉਬਾਰਿਯੈ ॥੪੧॥
922.t: kaamaka(n)dhalaa ek dhai sabh dhes ubaariyai ||41||
922.e: ‘To save your country, you handover Kaamkandla.’(41)
Chaupaee
Kamwati learned what the emissary had conveyed to Kam Sen.
The message from Bikrim had distressed the Raja.(42)
Dohira

922.g: ਨਿਸਿਸਿ ਚੜੇ ਦਿਨ ਕੇ ਭਏ ਨਿਸਿ ਰਵਿ ਕਰੈ ਉਦੋਤ ॥
922.t: nisis chaRe dhin ke bhe nis rav karai udhot ||
922.e: (Raja,) ‘Moon may shine during the day and sun may come at the night,

922.g: ਕਾਮਕੰਦਲਾ ਕੋ ਦਿਯਬ ਤਊ ਨ ਹਮ ਤੇ ਹੋਤ ॥੪੩॥
922.t: kaamaka(n)dhalaa ko dhiyab tuoo na ham te hot ||43||
922.e: ‘But I will not be able to give Kamkandla away.’(43)
Bhujang Chhand

922.g: ਸੁਨੋ ਰਾਜ ਕਹਾ ਨਾਰਿ ਕਾਮਾ ਬਿਚਾਰੀ ॥
922.t: suno raaj kahaa naar kaamaa bichaaree ||
922.e: (The emissary,) ‘Listen Raja, what magnificence is there in Kaamkandla,

922.g: ਕਹਾ ਗਾਠਿ ਬਾਧੀ ਤੁਮੈ ਜਾਨਿ ਪ੍ਯਾਰੀ ॥
922.t: kahaa gaaTh baadhee tumai jaan payaaree ||
922.e: ‘That you are protecting her tied to your own self,

922.g: ਕਹੀ ਮਾਨਿ ਮੇਰੀ ਕਹਾ ਨਾਹਿ ਭਾਖੋ ॥
922.t: kahee maan meree kahaa naeh bhaakho ||
922.e: ‘Beeding to my advice, don’t keep her with you,

922.g: ਇਨੈ ਦੈ ਮਿਲੌ ਤਾਹਿ ਕੌ ਗਰਬ ਰਾਖੋ ॥੪੪॥
922.t: einai dhai milau taeh kau garab raakho ||44||
922.e: ‘And by sending her away, protect your honour.(44)

922.g: ਹਠੀ ਹੈ ਹਮਾਰੀ ਸੁ ਤੁਮਹੂੰ ਪਛਾਨੋ ॥
922.t: haThee hai hamaaree su tumahoo(n) pachhaano ||

922.g: ਦਿਸਾ ਚਾਰਿ ਜਾ ਕੀ ਸਦਾ ਲੋਹ ਮਾਨੋ ॥
922.t: dhisaa chaar jaa kee sadhaa loh maano ||
922.e: ‘We persist and you must recognise, as our potency is known in all the four directions (of the world).’

922.g: ਬਲੀ ਦੇਵ ਆਦੇਵ ਜਾ ਕੌ ਬਖਾਨੈ ॥
922.t: balee dhev aadhev jaa kau bakhaanai ||

922.g: ਕਹਾ ਰੋਕ ਤੂ ਤੌਨ ਸੋ ਜੁਧੁ ਠਾਨੈ ॥੪੫॥
922.t: kahaa rok too tauan so judh Thaanai ||45||

922.g: ਜਬੈ ਦੂਤ ਕਟੁ ਬੈਨ ਐਸੇ ਉਚਾਰੇ ॥
922.t: jabai dhoot kaT bain aaise uchaare ||
922.e: The drums started to beat war cries when the emissary spoke harshly.

922.g: ਹਠਿਯੋ ਬੀਰ ਹਾਠੌ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਜੁਧ ਮੰਡੋ ॥
922.t: haThiyo beer haaThau kahiyo judh ma(n)ddo ||
922.e: The obstinate Raja pronounced the declaration of war and

922.g: ਕਹਾ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮਾ ਕਾਲ ਕੋ ਖੰਡ ਖੰਡੋ ॥੪੬॥
922.t: kahaa bikramaa kaal ko kha(n)dd kha(n)ddo ||46||
922.e: Determined to cut Bikrim into pieces.(46)

922.g: ਚੜਿਯੋ ਲੈ ਅਨੀ ਕੋ ਬਲੀ ਬੀਰ ਭਾਰੇ ॥
922.t: chaRiyo lai anee ko balee beer bhaare ||

922.e: Taking with him the brave Khandelas, Baghelas and Pandheras, he raided,

922.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੰਗ ਜੋਧਾ ਜਿਤੇ ਨਾਹਿ ਔਰੈ ॥੪੭॥
922.t: mahaa ja(n)g jodhaa jite naeh aauarai ||47||
922.e: And he had in his army Raharwars, Chohans and Ghalauts, who had taken part in great fighting.(47)

922.g: ਸੁਨ੍ਯੋ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮਾ ਬੀਰ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਬੁਲਾਏ ॥
922.t: sunayo bikramaa beer sabh hee bulaae ||

922.g: ਠਟੇ ਠਾਟ ਗਾੜੇ ਚਲੇ ਖੇਤ ਆਏ ॥
922.t: ThaTe ThaaT gaaRe chale khet aae ||
922.e: When jikrim heard the news, he collected all the intrepid ones.

922.g: ਦੁਹੂੰ ਓਰ ਤੇ ਸੂਰ ਸੈਨਾ ਉਮੰਗੈ ॥
922.t: dhuhoo(n) or te soor sainaa uma(n)gai ||
922.e: They both fought valiantly,

922.g: ਮਿਲੇ ਜਾਇ ਜਮੁਨਾ ਮਨੌ ਧਾਇ ਗੰਗੈ ॥੪੮॥
922.t: mile jai jamunaa manau dhai ga(n)gai ||48||
922.e: And amalgamated like river Jamuna and Gang.(48)

922.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਚਰਮ ਪੈ ਘਾਇ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਬਚਾਵੈ ॥
922.t: kite charam pai ghai taa ko bachaavai ||

922.g: ਕਿਤੋ ਬਰਮ ਪੈ ਚਰਮ ਰੁਪਿ ਗਰਮ ਝਾਰੈ ॥
922.t: kito baram pai charam rup garam jhaarai ||

923.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਸੂਲ ਸੈਥੀ ਸੂਆ ਹਾਥ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥
923.t: kite sool saithee sooaa haath lai kai ||

923.g: ਮੰਡੇ ਆਨਿ ਜੋਧਾ ਮਹਾ ਕੋਪ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਕੈ ॥੫੦॥
923.t: ma(n)dde aan jodhaa mahaa kop havai kai ||50||

923.g: ਫਰੀ ਧੋਪ ਖਾਡੇ ਲਏ ਫਾਸ ਐਸੀ ॥
923.t: faree dhop khaadde le faas aaisee ||

923.g: ਮਨੌ ਨਾਰਿ ਕੇ ਸਾਹੁ ਕੀ ਜੁਲਫ ਜੈਸੀ ॥
923.t: manau naar ke saahu kee julaf jaisee ||

923.g: ਕਰੀ ਮਤ ਕੀ ਭਾਤਿ ਮਾਰਤ ਬਿਹਾਰੈ ॥
923.t: karee mat kee bhaat maarat bihaarai ||

923.g: ਜਿਸੇ ਕੰਠਿ ਡਾਰੈ ਤਿਸੈ ਐਚ ਮਾਰੈ ॥੫੧॥
923.t: jise ka(n)Th ddaarai tisai aaich maarai ||51||

923.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
923.t: chauapiee ||
923.e: Chaupaee

923.g: ਜਬ ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਸਕਲ ਭਟ ਲਰੇ ॥
923.t: jab ieh bhaat sakal bhaT lare ||

923.g: ਟੂਕ ਟੂਕ ਰਨ ਮੈ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਪਰੇ ॥
923.t: Took Took ran mai havai pare ||
923.e: Fighting, and fighting hard, when they fell being cut in combats,

923.g: ਤਬ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਹਸਿ ਬੈਨ ਉਚਾਰੋ ॥
923.t: tab bikram has bain uchaaro ||

923.g: ਕਾਮਸੈਨ ਸੁਨੁ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਹਮਾਰੋ ॥੫੨॥
923.t: kaamasain sun kahiyo hamaaro ||52||
923.e: Bikrim came forward said smilingly, ‘Kam Dev, now listen to me,(52)

923.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
923.t: dhoharaa ||
923.e: Dohira

923.g: ਦੈ ਬੇਸ੍ਵਾ ਇਹ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਕੌ ਸੁਨੁ ਰੇ ਬਚਨ ਅਚੇਤ ॥
923.t: dhai besavaiaa ieh bipr kau sun re bachan achet ||
923.e: ‘Oh, fool, handover this prostitute to that Brahmin.

923.g: ਬ੍ਰਿਥਾ ਜੁਝਾਰਤ ਕ੍ਯੋ ਕਟਕ ਏਕ ਨਟੀ ਕੇ ਹੇਤ ॥੫੩॥
923.t: birathaa jujhaarat kayo kaTak ek naTee ke het ||53||
923.e: ‘Why for the sake of a prostitute, get your army killed.’(53)

923.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
923.t: chauapiee ||
923.e: Chaupaee

923.g: ਕਾਮਸੈਨ ਤਿਹ ਕਹੀ ਨ ਕਰੀ ॥
923.t: kaamasain teh kahee na karee ||

923.g: ਪੁਨਿ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਹਸਿ ਯਹੈ ਉਚਰੀ ॥
923.t: pun bikram has yahai ucharee ||
923.e: Kam Sen did not heed and Bikrim said,

923.g: ਹਮ ਤੁਮ ਲਰੈ ਕਪਟ ਤਜਿ ਦੋਈ ॥
923.t: ham tum larai kapaT taj dhoiee ||

923.g: ਕੈ ਜੀਤੇ ਕੈ ਹਾਰੈ ਕੋਈ ॥੫੪॥
923.t: kai jeete kai haarai koiee ||54||
923.e: ‘Whether one wins or losses, let us now fight.(54)

923.g: ਅਪਨੀ ਅਪਨੇ ਹੀ ਸਿਰ ਲੀਜੈ ॥
923.t: apanee apane hee sir leejai ||

923.g: ਔਰਨ ਕੇ ਸਿਰ ਬ੍ਰਿਥਾ ਨ ਦੀਜੈ ॥
923.t: aauaran ke sir birathaa na dheejai ||
923.e: ‘Let us finish our quarrel ourselves, why roll the heads of others. ‘For

923.g: ਬੈਠਿ ਬਿਗਾਰਿ ਆਪੁ ਜੋ ਕਰਿਯੈ ॥
923.t: baiTh bigaar aap jo kariyai ||

923.g: ਨਾਹਕ ਔਰ ਲੋਕ ਨਹਿ ਮਰਿਯੈ ॥੫੫॥
923.t: naahak aauar lok neh mariyai ||55||
923.e: Our own sake, we should not make others to lose their lives.’(55)

923.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
923.t: dhoharaa ||
923.e: Dohira

923.g: ਕਾਮਸੈਨ ਇਹ ਬਚਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਅਧਿਕ ਉਠਿਯੋ ਰਿਸ ਖਾਇ ॥
923.t: kaamasain ieh bachan sun adhik uThiyo ris khai ||
923.e: Listening to this, Kam Sen flew into the rage,

923.g: ਅਪਨੌ ਤੁਰੈ ਧਵਾਇ ਕੈ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਲਯੋ ਬੁਲਾਇ ॥੫੬॥
923.t: apanau turai dhavai kai bikram layo bulai ||56||
923.e: Sprinting his horse, he challenged Bikrim.(56)

923.g: ਕਾਮਸੈਨ ਐਸੇ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਸੂਰ ਸਾਮੁਹੇ ਜਾਇ ॥
923.t: kaamasain aaise kahiyo soor saamuhe jai ||
923.e: Kam Sen Addressed the Soldiers like this,

923.g: ਝਾਗਿ ਸੈਹਥੀ ਬ੍ਰਿਣ ਕਰੈ ਤੌ ਤੂ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਸਰਾਇ ॥੫੭॥
923.t: jhaag saihathee biran karai tau too bikram sarai ||57||
923.e: ‘I will consider you as Raja Bikrim, if you can injure me with the sword.’(57)

923.g: ਝਾਗਿ ਸੈਹਥੀ ਪੇਟ ਮਹਿ ਚਿਤ ਮਹਿ ਅਧਿਕ ਰਿਸਾਇ ॥
923.t: jhaag saihathee peT meh chit meh adhik risai ||

923.g: ਆਨਿ ਕਟਾਰੀ ਕੋ ਕਿਯੋ ਕਾਮਸੈਨ ਕੋ ਘਾਇ ॥੫੮॥
923.t: aan kaTaaree ko kiyo kaamasain ko ghai ||58||

923.g: ਐਸੇ ਕੌ ਐਸੋ ਲਹਤ ਜਿਯਤ ਨ ਛਾਡਤ ਔਰ ॥
923.t: aaise kau aaiso lahat jiyat na chhaaddat aauar ||
923.e: Tlien they struck each other with force,

923.g: ਮਾਰਿ ਕਟਾਰੀ ਰਾਖਿਯੋ ਜਿਯਤ ਰਾਵ ਤਿਹ ਠੌਰ ॥੫੯॥
923.t: maar kaTaaree raakhiyo jiyat raav teh Thauar ||59||
923.e: And, brandishing his sword he killed the Raja.(59)

923.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
923.t: chauapiee ||
923.e: Chaupaee

923.g: ਜੀਤਿ ਤਾਹਿ ਸਭ ਸੈਨ ਬੁਲਾਈ ॥
923.t: jeet taeh sabh sain bulaiee ||

923.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਕੀ ਬਜੀ ਬਧਾਈ ॥
923.t: bhaat bhaat kee bajee badhaiee ||
923.e: After the victory, he assembled his army and exchanged felicities.

923.g: ਦੇਵਨ ਰੀਝਿ ਇਹੈ ਬਰੁ ਦਯੋ ॥
923.t: dhevan reejh ihai bar dhayo ||

923.g: ਬ੍ਰਣੀ ਹੁਤੋ ਅਬ੍ਰਣ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਗਯੋ ॥੬੦॥
923.t: branee huto abran havai gayo ||60||
923.e: The gods showered their blessing and Bikrim’s injuries Were diminished.(60)

923.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
923.t: dhoharaa ||
923.e: Dohira

923.g: ਅਥਿਤ ਭੇਖ ਸਜਿ ਆਪੁ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਗਯੋ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਕੇ ਕਾਮ ॥
923.t: athit bhekh saj aap nirap gayo bipr ke kaam ||
923.e: Disguising himself as Brahmin priest, he went there,

923.g: ਜਹ ਕਾਮਾ ਲੋਟਤ ਹੁਤੀ ਲੈ ਮਾਧਵ ਕੋ ਨਾਮ ॥੬੧॥
923.t: jeh kaamaa loTat hutee lai maadhav ko naam ||61||
923.e: Where Kama was rolling in remembrance of Madhwan.

923.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
923.t: chauapiee ||
923.e: Chaupaee

923.g: ਜਾਤੈ ਇਹੈ ਬਚਨ ਤਿਨ ਕਹਿਯੋ ॥
923.t: jaatai ihai bachan tin kahiyo ||

923.g: ਮਾਧਵ ਖੇਤ ਹੇਤ ਤਵ ਰਹਿਯੋ ॥
923.t: maadhav khet het tav rahiyo ||
923.e: Raja (Bikrim) told her that Madhwan had died in the war.

923.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਬਚਨ ਤਬ ਹੀ ਮਰਿ ਗਈ ॥
923.t: sunat bachan tab hee mar giee ||

923.g: ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਲੈ ਇਹੈ ਖਬਰਿ ਦਿਜ ਦਈ ॥੬੨॥
923.t: nirap lai ihai khabar dhij dhiee ||62||
923.e: Hearing the news she immediately breathed her last and then Raja went to give the news to Brahmin.(62)

923.g: ਯਹ ਬਚ ਜਬ ਸ੍ਰੋਨਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਲੀਨੋ ॥
923.t: yeh bach jab sronan sun leeno ||

923.g: ਪਲਕ ਏਕ ਮਹਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਨਹਿ ਦੀਨੋ ॥
923.t: palak ek meh praaneh dheeno ||
923.e: When he (Brahmin) heard this news through his own ears, he, instantly, expired.

923.g: ਜਬ ਕੌਤਕ ਇਹ ਰਾਇ ਨਿਹਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
923.t: jab kauatak ieh rai nihaariyo ||

924.e: When Raja witnessed this, he decided to immolate himself as well.(63)
When the flaming pyre was ready, suddenly Betaal, (his court poet) appeared.

924.g: ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਕੇ ਚਿਤ ਕੋ ਤਾਪੁ ਮਿਟਾਯੋ ॥੬੪॥
924.t: nirap ke chit ko taap miTaayo ||64||
924.e: He sprinkled the nectar over the bodies of both of them, made them alive again and eliminated Raja’s affliction.(64)
Dohira

924.g: ਸਹਿ ਸੈਥੀ ਪਾਵਕ ਬਰਿਯੋ ਦੁਹੂੰਅਨ ਲਯੋ ਬਚਾਇ ॥
924.t: seh saithee paavak bariyo dhuhoo(n)an layo bachai ||
924.e: He bore the brunt of sword and had decided to burn himself,

924.g: ਕਾਮਾ ਦਈ ਦਿਜੋਤ ਮਹਿ ਧੰਨ੍ਯ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮਾਰਾਇ ॥੬੫॥
924.t: kaamaa dhiee dhijot meh dha(n)nay bikramaarai ||65||
924.e: Raja Bikrim, the endower of life to Kama is meritorious.(65)(l)

924.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਪੁਰਖ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਇਕਾਨਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੯੧॥੧੬੩੪॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
924.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane purakh charitre ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe ikaanavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||91||1634||afajoo(n)||
924.e: Ninety-first Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (91)(1632)
Chaupaee
In the south, the women were so pretty that even the yogis, the ascetics, gone there, had became householders.

924.g: ਸਭ ਅਰਿ ਕੁਲ ਜਾ ਤੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਣ ਗਹਈ ॥੧॥
924.t: sabh ar kul jaa te tiran gahiee ||1||
924.e: Mangal Sen was the Raja of that part and all the enemies dreaded of his power.(1)

924.g: ਸਰੂਪ ਕਲਾ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਬਰ ਨਾਰੀ ॥
924.t: saroop kalaa taa kee bar naaree ||

924.e: Saroup Kala was his wife who was as pretty as (the legendry) wife of

924.g: ਤਾ ਸੋ ਨੇਹ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਕੋ ਰਹੈ ॥
924.t: taa so neh nirapat ko rahai ||

924.e: Shiva. Raja loved her intensively and performed his duties according to her wishes.(2)
Ruaamal Chhand

924.g: ਰੰਗ ਮਹਲ ਬਿਖੈ ਹੁਤੇ ਨਰ ਰਾਇ ਤਵਨੈ ਕਾਲ ॥
924.t: ra(n)g mahal bikhai hute nar rai tavanai kaal ||

924.g: ਰੂਪ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਬਿਰਾਜਤੀ ਤਹ ਸੁੰਦਰੀ ਲੈ ਬਾਲ ॥
924.t: roop prabhaa biraajatee teh su(n)dharee lai baal ||
924.e: When Raja was in the Palace, Roop Prabha used to come there with her companions.

924.g: ਕਾਨ੍ਰਹਰੇ ਨਾਦ ਔ ਨਫੀਰੀ ਬੇਨੁ ਬੀਨ ਮ੍ਰਿਦੰਗ ॥
924.t: kaanrahare naadh aau nafeeree ben been miradha(n)g ||

924.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਕੁਲਾਹਲ ਹੋਤ ਨਾਨਾ ਰੰਗ ॥੩॥
924.t: bhaat bhaatin ke kulaahal hot naanaa ra(n)g ||3||
924.e: The musical notes of Raag Kanrra were melodiously played on Nafiris, the flutes and the ecstasies were showered.(3)

924.g: ਏਕ ਨਟੂਆ ਤਹ ਰਹੈ ਤਿਹ ਬਿਸੁਨ ਦਤ੍ਵਾ ਨਾਮ ॥
924.t: ek naTooaa teh rahai teh bisun dhatavaiaa naam ||
924.e: There lived a bard who was known as Bishan Datt,

924.g: ਰਾਵ ਜੂ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਨਚਾਵਤ ਰਹੈ ਆਠੌ ਜਾਮ ॥
924.t: raav joo taa kau nachaavat rahai aaThau jaam ||
924.e: Whom the Raja had made to dance whole day long.

924.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਰੂਪ ਬਿਲੋਕਿ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਰਾਨਿਯਹਿ ਨਿਜੁ ਨੈਨ ॥
924.t: amit roop bilok taa kau raaniyeh nij nain ||
924.e: When the Rani saw him with her own eyes,

924.g: ਹ੍ਵੈ ਗਿਰੀ ਬਿਸੰਭਾਰ ਭੂ ਪੈ ਬਧੀ ਸਾਯਕ ਮੈਨ ॥੪॥
924.t: havai giree bisa(n)bhaar bhoo pai badhee saayak main ||4||
924.e: She was overpower with lust and fell flat on the ground.(4)
Tomar Chhand
The Rani sent her maid and called him to her home.
Ignoring the prestige of the Raja, she indulged in love-making with him.(5)
His extreme handsomeness had shot through her a Cupid’s sharp arrow.
In the meantime, the Raja appeared.(6)
She proceeded this way: she sent for it large cooking-vessel,
And covered it with a lid so that no one could see inside.(7)
(She spoke) ‘I have filled it with water and not a drop can drip out of it,
‘I have put roses in it,’ and then she presented her husband the rosewater.(8)
Dohira

924.g: ਸੀਂਚ੍ਰਯੋ ਵਹੈ ਗੁਲਾਬ ਲੈ ਪਤਿ ਕੀ ਪਗਿਯਾ ਮਾਹਿ ॥
924.t: see(n)chrayo vahai gulaab lai pat kee pagiyaa maeh ||
924.e: She took some rose-water, and sprinkled it on her husband’s turban.

924.g: ਛਿਰਕਿ ਸਭਨ ਪਹਿ ਕਾਢਿਯੌ ਭੇਦ ਲਹਿਯੋ ਜੜ ਨਾਹਿ ॥੯॥
924.t: chhirak sabhan peh kaaddiyau bhedh lahiyo jaR naeh ||9||
924.e: Under the shower of rose-water she slipped him out and no one could acquiesce the real secret.
Chaupaee

925.g: ਨਾਥ ਬਾਗ ਜੋ ਮੈ ਲਗਵਾਯੋ ॥
925.t: naath baag jo mai lagavaayo ||
925.e: ‘My Master, the garden, which I have fostered,

925.g: ਯਹ ਗੁਲਾਬ ਤਿਹ ਠਾ ਤੇ ਆਯੋ ॥
925.t: yeh gulaab teh Thaa te aayo ||
925.e: ‘These roses have come out ofthat.

925.g: ਸਕਲ ਸਖਿਨ ਜੁਤ ਤੁਮ ਪੈ ਡਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
925.t: sakal sakhin jut tum pai ddaariyo ||
925.e: ‘We, all the compatriots, have made the selection.’

925.g: ਪ੍ਰਫੁਲਤ ਭਯੋ ਜੜ ਕਛੁ ਨ ਬਿਚਾਰਿਯੋ ॥੧੦॥
925.t: prafulat bhayo jaR kachh na bichaariyo ||10||
925.e: Listening to this, that fool was overjoyed.(l0)(1)

925.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਬਾਨਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੯੨॥੧੬੪੪॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
925.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitre ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe baanavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||92||1644||afajoo(n)||
925.e: Ninety-second Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (92)(1642)

925.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
925.t: dhoharaa ||
925.e: Dohira

925.g: ਚਲਿਯੋ ਜੁਲਾਹੋ ਸਾਹੁਰੇ ਉਡਿ ਜਾ ਕਹਤਾ ਜਾਇ ॥
925.t: chaliyo julaaho saahure udd jaa kahataa jai ||
925.e: A weaver was walking to his in-laws and kept on shoUting, ‘flyaway’

925.g: ਬਧਿਕਨ ਕੁਸਗੁਨ ਜਾਨਿ ਕੈ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ਤਾਹਿ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੧॥
925.t: badhikan kusagun jaan kai maariyo taeh banai ||1||
925.e: A hunter considering this to be a bad omen beat him up.(1)

925.g: ਬਧਿਕ ਬਾਚ ॥
925.t: badhik baach ||
925.e: Badhik Talk

925.g: ਉਡਿ ਉਡਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਫਾਸਿਯਹੁ ਸੌ ਕਹਤਾ ਮਗੁ ਜਾਇ ॥
925.t: audd udd aavahu faasiyahu sau kahataa mag jai ||
925.e: (The hunter told him) ‘You must say come flying and get entrapped.

925.g: ਜੋ ਐਸੋ ਬਚ ਪੁਨਿ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਹਨਿਹੈ ਤੋਹਿ ਰਿਸਾਇ ॥੨॥
925.t: jo aaiso bach pun kahiyo hanihai toh risai ||2||
925.e: ‘If you shout other way, I will get furious and kill you’.(2)

925.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
925.t: chauapiee ||
925.e: Chaupaee

925.g: ਫਸਿ ਫਸਿ ਜਾਵਹੁ ਉਡਿ ਉਡਿ ਆਇ ॥
925.t: fas fas jaavahu udd udd aai ||

925.g: ਐਸੇ ਕਹਤ ਜੁਲਾਹੋ ਜਾਇ ॥
925.t: aaise kahat julaaho jai ||
925.e: Then he started his journey saying, ‘Come flying and get entrapped.’

925.g: ਚੋਰਨ ਕੁਸਗੁਨ ਚਿਤ ਬਿਚਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
925.t: choran kusagun chit bichaariyo ||

925.g: ਦੋ ਸੈ ਜੁਤੀ ਸੌ ਤਿਹ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ॥੩॥
925.t: dho sai jutee sau teh maariyo ||3||
925.e: This was heard by the thieves and they hit him with shoes two hundred times.(3 )

925.g: ਚੋਰਨ ਬਾਚ ॥
925.t: choran baach ||
925.e: Thieve’s Instruction

925.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
925.t: dhoharaa ||
925.e: Dohira

925.g: ਲੈ ਆਵਹੁ ਧਰਿ ਜਾਇਯਹੁ ਯੌ ਕਹਿ ਕਰੌ ਪਯਾਨ ॥
925.t: lai aavahu dhar jaiyahu yau keh karau payaan ||
925.e: ‘Say, “Bring in here, leave and go away.”

925.g: ਜੋ ਉਹਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਬਖਾਨਿਹੋ ਹਨਿਹੈ ਤੁਹਿ ਤਨ ਬਾਨ ॥੪॥
925.t: jo uh bhaat bakhaaniho hanihai tuh tan baan ||4||
925.e: “If you speak otherwise, we will kill you.”(4)

925.g: ਜਬ ਚੋਰਨ ਐਸੇ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਤਬ ਤਾ ਤੇ ਡਰ ਪਾਇ ॥
925.t: jab choran aaise kahiyo tab taa te ddar pai ||
925.e: When afraid of thieves he walked asserting,

925.g: ਲੈ ਆਵਹੁ ਧਰਿ ਜਾਇਯਹੁ ਯੌ ਮਗੁ ਕਹਤੌ ਜਾਇ ॥੫॥
925.t: lai aavahu dhar jaiyahu yau mag kahatau jai ||5||
925.e: ‘Bring it here, leave it and go away.’(5)

925.g: ਚਾਰ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹ ਕੇ ਇਕ ਨੈ ਤਜਾ ਪਰਾਨ ॥
925.t: chaar putr paatisaeh ke ik nai tajaa paraan ||
925.e: A Raja had four sons. One had just breathed his last,

925.g: ਦਾਬਨ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਲੈ ਚਲੇ ਅਧਿਕ ਸੋਕ ਮਨ ਮਾਨਿ ॥੬॥
925.t: dhaaban taa kau lai chale adhik sok man maan ||6||
925.e: And they were taking him for burial.(6)

925.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
925.t: chauapiee ||
925.e: Chaupaee

925.g: ਤਬ ਲੌ ਕਹਤ ਜੁਲਾਹੋ ਐਯਹੁ ॥
925.t: tab lau kahat julaaho aaiyahu ||

925.g: ਲੈ ਲੈ ਆਵਹੁ ਧਰ ਧਰ ਜੈਯਹੁ ॥
925.t: lai lai aavahu dhar dhar jaiyahu ||
925.e: They met the weaver who was saying, ‘Bring in and put it there.’

925.g: ਸੈਨਾ ਕੇ ਸ੍ਰਵਨਨ ਯਹ ਪਰੀ ॥
925.t: sainaa ke sravanan yeh paree ||

925.g: ਪੰਦ੍ਰਹ ਸੈ ਪਨਹੀ ਤਹ ਝਰੀ ॥੭॥
925.t: pa(n)dhreh sai panahee teh jharee ||7||
925.e: When the Raja’s soldiers heard this, they gave him beating of fifteen hundred shoes,(7)

925.g: ਤਿਨ ਸੋ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਕਹੋ ਸੁ ਉਚਾਰੋ ॥
925.t: tin so kahiyo kaho su uchaaro ||

925.g: ਕਹਿਯੋ ਬੁਰਾ ਭਯੋ ਕਹਤ ਪਧਾਰੋ ॥
925.t: kahiyo buraa bhayo kahat padhaaro ||
925.e: They instructed him to repeat, ‘What a bad thing has happened.’

925.g: ਭੇਦ ਅਭੇਦ ਕੀ ਬਾਤ ਨ ਜਾਨੀ ॥
925.t: bhedh abhedh kee baat na jaanee ||

925.g: ਜੋ ਤਿਨ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਵਹੈ ਜੜ ਮਾਨੀ ॥੮॥
925.t: jo tin kahiyo vahai jaR maanee ||8||
925.e: He (weaver) did not grasp why had they told him to say so.(8)

925.g: ਏਕ ਰਾਵ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਬਹੁ ਨਾਰੀ ॥
925.t: ek raav taa ke bahu naaree ||

925.g: ਪੂਤ ਨ ਹੋਤ ਤਾਹਿ ਦੁਖ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
925.t: poot na hot taeh dhukh bhaaree ||
925.e: There was one Raja he had many wives but no son.

925.g: ਔਰ ਬ੍ਯਾਹਿ ਬ੍ਯਾਕੁਲ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਕੀਨੋ ॥
925.t: aauar bayaeh bayaakul havai keeno ||

925.g: ਤਾ ਕੇ ਭਵਨ ਪੂਤ ਬਿਧਿ ਦੀਨੋ ॥੯॥
925.t: taa ke bhavan poot bidh dheeno ||9||
925.e: He married another woman and God bestowed him with a son.(9)

925.g: ਸਭਹਿਨ ਆਨੰਦ ਚਿਤ ਬਢਾਯੋ ॥
925.t: sabhahin aana(n)dh chit baddaayo ||

925.g: ਤਬ ਲੌ ਕਹਤ ਜੁਲਾਹੋ ਆਯੋ ॥
925.t: tab lau kahat julaaho aayo ||
925.e: Every body was very happy when the weaver passed by.

925.g: ਬੁਰਾ ਭਯੋ ਕਹਿ ਊਚ ਪੁਕਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
925.t: buraa bhayo keh uooch pukaariyo ||

925.g: ਸੁਨ੍ਯੋ ਜਾਹਿ ਪਨਹਿਨ ਤਿਨ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ॥੧੦॥
925.t: sunayo jaeh panahin tin maariyo ||10||
925.e: ‘What a bad thing has happened’, he said, and he was given beating by the Raja.(10)

925.g: ਪੁਰ ਜਨ ਬਾਚ ॥
925.t: pur jan baach ||

925.g: ਭਲਾ ਭਯੋ ਇਹ ਕਹਤ ਪਧਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
925.t: bhalaa bhayo ieh kahat padhaariyo ||

925.g: ਜਬ ਲੋਗਨ ਜੂਤਿਨ ਸੋ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
925.t: jab logan jootin so maariyo ||
925.e: After getting thrashing by every body he was told to say, ‘It is God’s blessing.’

925.g: ਜਾਤ ਭਯੋ ਤਿਹ ਠਾ ਬਡਭਾਗੀ ॥
925.t: jaat bhayo teh Thaa baddabhaagee ||

925.g: ਜਹ ਅਤਿ ਅਗਨਿ ਨਗਰ ਮਹਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥੧੧॥
925.t: jeh at agan nagar meh laagee ||11||
925.e: Then he reached a village, which was on fire.(11)

925.g: ਗਿਰਿ ਗਿਰਿ ਪਰੈ ਮਹਲ ਜਹ ਭਾਰੇ ॥
925.t: gir gir parai mahal jeh bhaare ||

925.g: ਛਪਰਨ ਕੇ ਜਹ ਉਡੈ ਅਵਾਰੇ ॥
925.t: chhaparan ke jeh uddai avaare ||
925.e: Huge palaces were even crumbling, and the roofs were flying away.

926.e: The fool said, “It is God’s blessing”, and when the people heart this they beat him up.(12)
Dohira

926.g: ਦਸ ਹਜਾਰ ਪਨਹੀਨ ਕੀ ਸਹੀ ਜੁਲਾਹੇ ਮਾਰਿ ॥
926.t: dhas hajaar panaheen kee sahee julaahe maar ||
926.e: After getting the beating of more than ten thousand shoes,

926.g: ਤਾ ਪਾਛੈ ਪਹੁਚਤ ਭਯੋ ਜਹਾ ਹੁਤੀ ਸਸੁਰਾਰਿ ॥੧੩॥
926.t: taa paachhai pahuchat bhayo jahaa hutee sasuraar ||13||
926.e: The weaver reached the house of his in-laws.(13)
Chaupaee

926.g: ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਜਨ ਕਹਾ ਖਾਹੁ ਨਹਿ ਖਾਵੈ ॥
926.t: gireh jan kahaa khaahu neh khaavai ||

926.e: ‘The house people offered him food but he did not eat and went to sleep empty stomach.
When half the night had passed, the hunger tormented him.(l4)
Bolding a stick he broke the pitcher and drank all the water.
The Sun rose, the stars went away and he took in his hands the weavers’ wefts.(15)
Dohira

926.g: ਤਾਨੀ ਬੇਚਿ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਨ ਲੀ ਚਲਿਯੋ ਚਾਕਰੀ ਧਾਇ ॥
926.t: taanee bech kirapaan lee chaliyo chaakaree dhai ||
926.e: Be bartered the wefts, acquired a sword and marched again.

926.g: ਮਾਰਤ ਮਾਰਗ ਸਿੰਘ ਜਹ ਤਿਹ ਠਾ ਪਹੁਚ੍ਯੋ ਜਾਇ ॥੧੬॥
926.t: maarat maarag si(n)gh jeh teh Thaa pahuchayo jai ||16||
926.e: Be reached the place where a lion used to plunder the people and eat them.(16)

926.g: ਤ੍ਰਸਿਤ ਜੁਲਾਹੋ ਦ੍ਰੁਮ ਚੜ੍ਯੋ ਗਹੈ ਸੈਹਥੀ ਹਾਥ ॥
926.t: trasit julaaho dhrum chaRayo gahai saihathee haath ||
926.e: Being afraid, holding the sword in his hand, he went up the tree.

926.g: ਤਰੇ ਆਨਿ ਠਾਢੋ ਭਯੋ ਸਿੰਘ ਰੋਸ ਕੇ ਸਾਥ ॥੧੭॥
926.t: tare aan Thaaddo bhayo si(n)gh ros ke saath ||17||
926.e: And down there the lion, which was right furious, took his place.(l7)
Chaupaee
When the lion looked up at the weaver, he trembled and the sword fell from his hands.

926.g: ਮੁਖ ਮੈ ਲਗੀ ਪਿਸਟਿ ਤਰ ਨਿਕਸੀ ॥
926.t: mukh mai lagee pisaT tar nikasee ||

926.e: It went right into the mOUth of the lion and came out ofthe stomach.(18)
When he observed that the lion was dead,
He came down, cut the ear and the tail and showed to the Raja to claim more wages.(l9)
Dohira

926.g: ਏਕ ਸਤ੍ਰੁ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਹੁਤੋ ਚੜਿਯੋ ਅਨੀ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
926.t: ek satr taa ko huto chaRiyo anee banai ||
926.e: The Raja had an enemy, who had raided him.

926.g: ਸੈਨਾਪਤਿ ਪਚਮਾਰ ਕੈ ਇਹ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਦਿਯੋ ਪਠਾਇ ॥੨੦॥
926.t: sainaapat pachamaar kai ieh nirap dhiyo paThai ||20||
926.e: Reflecting on his bravery Raja appointed him as the supreme commander.(20)
Chaupaee
When the weaver heard this news, he called his wife.

926.g: ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਅਧਿਕ ਦੁਹੂੰ ਡਰ ਕੀਨੋ ॥
926.t: chit mai adhik dhuhoo(n) ddar keeno ||

926.g: ਅਰਧ ਰਾਤਿ ਬਨ ਕੋ ਮਗੁ ਲੀਨੋ ॥੨੧॥
926.t: aradh raat ban ko mag leeno ||21||
926.e: Both were terror stricken and, at the pitch of the night, took their way to the jungle.(21)

926.g: ਤਬ ਹੀ ਘੋਰ ਘਟਾ ਘਨ ਗਾਜ੍ਰਯੋ ॥
926.t: tab hee ghor ghaTaa ghan gaajrayo ||
926.e: When the weaver and his wife were running away, the thunder storm approached,
And amidst the severe lightning, they lost their way.(22)

926.g: ਮਗ ਤੈ ਭੂਲਿ ਤਿਸੀ ਮਗੁ ਪਰਿਯੋ ॥
926.t: mag tai bhool tisee mag pariyo ||

926.g: ਜਹ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਅਰਿ ਕੋ ਲਸਕਰ ਢਰਿਯੋ ॥
926.t: jeh nirap ar ko lasakar ddariyo ||
926.e: Losing their way they came to the place where the Raja’s enemy were encamping.
There was a, well which was not visible to them and the weaver fell in it.(23)
Dohira

926.g: ਜਬ ਤਾਹੀ ਕੂੰਈ ਬਿਖੈ ਜਾਇ ਪਰਿਯੋ ਬਿਸੰਭਾਰ ॥
926.t: jab taahee koo(n)iee bikhai jai pariyo bisa(n)bhaar ||
926.e: When he fell in the well, became unconscious,

926.g: ਤਬ ਐਸੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕਹਿ ਉਠੀ ਆਨਿ ਪਰਿਯੋ ਪਚਮਾਰ ॥੨੪॥
926.t: tab aaise tiray keh uThee aan pariyo pachamaar ||24||
926.e: Then the woman shoUted, ‘My dear lion killer has fallen there.’(24)
Arril

927.g: ਆਨਿ ਪਰਿਯੋ ਪਚਮਾਰ ਸਭਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਪਾਇਯੋ ॥
927.t: aan pariyo pachamaar sabhan sun paiyo ||
927.e: Ever body heard that the lion killer was there.

927.g: ਅਤਿ ਲਸਕਰ ਚਿਤ ਮਾਹਿ ਸੁ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਬਢਾਇਯੋ ॥
927.t: at lasakar chit maeh su traas baddaiyo ||
927.e: The whole (enemy) army was panicked with fear.

927.g: ਲੋਹ ਅਧਿਕ ਤਿਨ ਮਾਹਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਐਸੀ ਪਰਿਯੋ ॥
927.t: loh adhik tin maeh bhaat aaisee pariyo ||
927.e: They started to fight with each other,

927.g: ਹੋ ਜੋਧਾ ਤਿਨ ਤੇ ਏਕ ਨ ਜਿਯਤੇ ਉਬਰਿਯੋ ॥੨੫॥
927.t: ho jodhaa tin te ek na jiyate ubariyo ||25||
927.e: And none of them was saved.(25)
Dohira

927.g: ਪੂਤ ਪਿਤਾ ਕੇ ਸਿਰ ਦਈ ਪਿਤਾ ਪੂਤ ਸਿਰ ਮਾਹਿ ॥
927.t: poot pitaa ke sir dhiee pitaa poot sir maeh ||
927.e: (In the melee) Even the father killed the son and the son killed the father,

927.g: ਇਸੀ ਭਾਤਿ ਸਭ ਕਟਿ ਮਰੇ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਸੁਭਟ ਕੋਊ ਨਾਹਿ ॥੨੬॥
927.t: eisee bhaat sabh kaT mare rahiyo subhaT kouoo naeh ||26||
927.e: And this way they all cut each other and no fighter was left behind.(26)
Chaupaee
Then the weaver-woman came and told the Raja what had happened.

927.g: ਜਬ ਯਹ ਭੇਦ ਰਾਵ ਸੁਨਿ ਪਾਯੋ ॥
927.t: jab yeh bhedh raav sun paayo ||

927.e: When the Raja learned the secret, he sent palanquin and honoured the weaver.(27)(1)

927.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਤਿਰਾਨਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੯੩॥੧੬੭੧॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
927.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitre ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe tiraanavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||93||1671||afajoo(n)||
927.e: Ninety-third Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (93)(J669)
Dohira

927.g: ਚਾਦਨ ਹੂੰ ਕੇ ਦੇਸ ਮੈ ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਚਾਦ ਪੁਰ ਗਾਉ ॥
927.t: chaadhan hoo(n) ke dhes mai pragaT chaadh pur gaau ||
927.e: In the country of Chandan, there was a town called Chandanpur.

927.g: ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਏਕ ਤਿਹ ਠਾ ਰਹੈ ਦੀਨ ਦਯਾਲ ਤਿਹ ਨਾਉ ॥੧॥
927.t: bipr ek teh Thaa rahai dheen dhayaal teh naau ||1||
927.e: There used to live a Brahmin priest, whose name was Din Diaal.(1)
Chaupaee
The woman from various countries came there and paid their obeisance to the Brahmin.
All of them used to recite celestial hymns as he seemed to them as the epitome of Cupid.(2)
Dohira

927.g: ਏਕ ਨਾਰਿ ਤਿਹ ਠਾ ਹੁਤੀ ਰਤਿ ਸਮ ਰੂਪ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
927.t: ek naar teh Thaa hutee rat sam roop apaar ||
927.e: There used to live a woman who was embodiment of the Cupid’s consort.

927.g: ਸੋ ਯਾ ਪੈ ਅਟਕਤ ਭਈ ਰਤਿ ਪਤਿ ਤਾਹਿ ਬਿਚਾਰ ॥੩॥
927.t: so yaa pai aTakat bhiee rat pat taeh bichaar ||3||
927.e: Considering him to be the Cupid, she wrapped herself around him.(3)
Chaupaee

927.g: ਕਬਹੂੰ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਆਵੈ ॥
927.t: kabahoo(n) tiray taa ke gireh aavai ||

927.e: Now the woman started either to come to him or call him over.

927.g: ਏਕ ਦਿਵਸ ਦਿਨ ਕੌ ਵਹੁ ਆਯੋ ॥
927.t: ek dhivas dhin kau vahu aayo ||

927.e: Once, during the day he came and the woman displayed this trick.(4)
Savaiyya

927.g: ਬੈਠੀ ਹੁਤੀ ਸਖੀ ਮਧਿ ਅਲੀਨ ਮੌ ਦੀਨ ਦਯਾਲ ਸੌ ਨੇਹੁ ਨਵੀਨੋ ॥
927.t: baiThee hutee sakhee madh aleen mau dheen dhayaal sau neh naveeno ||
927.e: She was sitting with her friends and saying that she loved Din Diaal.

927.g: ਬੈਨਨਿ ਚਿੰਤ ਕਰੈ ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਇਤ ਨੈਨਨਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਕੋ ਮਨੁ ਲੀਨੋ ॥
927.t: bainan chi(n)t karai chit mai it nainan preetam ko man leeno ||
927.e: Although she was conversing sitting there, her mind was at the thought of her paramour.

927.g: ਨੈਨ ਕੀ ਕਾਲ ਕੋ ਬੀਚਲ ਦੇਖਿ ਸੁ ਸੁੰਦਰਿ ਘਾਤ ਚਿਤੈਬੇ ਕੋ ਕੀਨੋ ॥
927.t: nain kee kaal ko beechal dhekh su su(n)dhar ghaat chitaibe ko keeno ||
927.e: With askance looks she pointed her beautiful (friends) at him,

927.g: ਹੀ ਲਖਿ ਪਾਇ ਜੰਭਾਇ ਲਈ ਚੁਟਕੀ ਚਟਕਾਇ ਬਿਦਾ ਕਰਿ ਦੀਨੋ ॥੫॥
927.t: hee lakh pai ja(n)bhai liee chuTakee chaTakai bidhaa kar dheeno ||5||
927.e: She yawned and with the snap ofthe fingers pointed him to go.(5)(1)

927.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਚੌਰਾਨਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੯੪॥੧੬੭੬॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
927.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitre ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe chauaraanavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||94||1676||afajoo(n)||
927.e: Ninety-four Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (94)(1676)
Chaupaee
There was a daughter of a Jat, the peasant, she came to us for begging.
She called herself as Bindo; she was an accomplice of the thieves.(1)
She took an earthen-pitcher and put in it linseeds.
After putting four nails in it, she buried it (at the back ofthe place).(2)

927.g: ਇਕੁ ਟੌਨਾ ਇਹ ਕਰ ਮਮ ਆਯੋ ॥
927.t: eik Tauanaa ieh kar mam aayo ||
927.e: She came and told the Raja, ‘Some maid has performed an incantation.

927.g: ਜੋ ਤੁਮ ਕਹੋ ਤੋ ਆਨਿ ਦਿਖਾਊ ॥
927.t: jo tum kaho to aan dhikhaauoo ||

927.g: ਕਛੁ ਮੁਖ ਤੇ ਆਗ੍ਯਾ ਤਵ ਪਾਊ ॥੩॥
927.t: kachh mukh te aagayaa tav paauoo ||3||
927.e: ‘If you desire and order yourself, and I will display it to you.’(3)
She took Raja and showed him and put all the people in whim.

927.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਭੇਦ ਨ ਕਿਨਹੂੰ ਜਾਨ੍ਯੋ ॥੪॥
927.t: taa ko bhedh na kinahoo(n) jaanayo ||4||
927.e: She proved it to be true and none could acquiesce her trick.(4)
When the backbiting reacted, the Raja summoned that maid.

927.g: ਸੀ ਨ ਮੁਖ ਤੇ ਨੈਕ ਉਚਾਰੀ ॥੫॥
927.t: see na mukh te naik uchaaree ||5||
927.e: She was beaten with whips but she did not murmur.(5)

927.g: ਮਾਰਿ ਪਰੀ ਵਹ ਨੈਕੁ ਨ ਮਾਨ੍ਯੋ ॥
927.t: maar paree veh naik na maanayo ||

927.e: In spite of beating she did not confess and the Raja thought she was stubborn.

927.g: ਦਿਬ ਕੀ ਬਾਤ ਚਲਨ ਜਬ ਲਾਗੀ ॥
927.t: dhib kee baat chalan jab laagee ||

927.e: At the night when they were discussing, she ran away.(6)
The Raja sent guards to catch her and put her in the cell.
He made her to take poison and dispatched her to the domain of death.(7)(1)

927.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਪਚਾਨਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੯੫॥੧੬੮੩॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
927.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitre ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe pachaanavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||95||1683||afajoo(n)||
927.e: Ninety-fifth Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (95)(1681)
Dohira

927.g: ਮਰਗ ਜੌਹਡੇ ਕੇ ਬਿਖੈ ਏਕ ਪਠਾਨੀ ਨਾਰ ॥
927.t: marag jauahadde ke bikhai ek paThaanee naar ||
927.e: In the city of Marg Johda, a woman of Path an decent used to live.

927.g: ਬੈਰਮ ਖਾ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਰਹੈ ਭਰਤਾ ਅਤਿ ਸੁਭ ਕਾਰ ॥੧॥
927.t: bairam khaa taa ko rahai bharataa at subh kaar ||1||
927.e: Bairam Khan was her husband who always revelled in good causes.(1)

927.g: ਤਵਨ ਪਠਾਨੀ ਕੋ ਹੁਤੋ ਨਾਮ ਗੌਹਰਾ ਰਾਇ ॥
927.t: tavan paThaanee ko huto naam gauaharaa rai ||
927.e: The name of the Pathani, the Pathan’s woman, was Gohraan Raae,

927.g: ਜਾਨੁ ਕਨਕ ਕੀ ਪੁਤ੍ਰਿਕਾ ਬਿਧਨਾ ਰਚੀ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੨॥
927.t: jaan kanak kee putirakaa bidhanaa rachee banai ||2||
927.e: And she was, as if, the creation of Brahma, the God, Himself.(2)

927.g: ਅਰਿ ਬਲੁ ਕੈ ਆਵਤ ਭਏ ਤਾ ਪੈ ਅਤਿ ਦਲ ਜੋਰਿ ॥
927.t: ar bal kai aavat bhe taa pai at dhal jor ||
927.e: The enemy raided with great force and power,

927.g: ਦੈ ਹੈ ਯਾਹਿ ਨਿਕਾਰਿ ਕੈ ਲੈ ਹੈ ਦੇਸ ਮਰੋਰਿ ॥੩॥
927.t: dhai hai yaeh nikaar kai lai hai dhes maror ||3||
927.e: To capture the country and took her away.(3)

928.e: Chaupaee
The emissary came to Bairam and demonstrated his anger.
‘You, the unlucky one, are sitting idle and the enemy is here with his guns.’(4)
Bairam was scared and decided to run away,

928.g: ਤਾ ਸੋ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਸੁ ਚਹੌ ਸੁਨਾਈ ॥੫॥
928.t: taa so kahiyo su chahau sunaiee ||5||
928.e: Then the Pathani came forward and said to him,(5)
Dohira

928.g: ਤੋਰ ਪਿਤਾ ਐਸੋ ਹੁਤੋ ਜਾ ਕੋ ਜਗ ਮੈ ਨਾਮ ॥
928.t: tor pitaa aaiso huto jaa ko jag mai naam ||
928.e: ‘Your father was renowned all over the world,

928.g: ਤੂ ਕਾਤਰ ਐਸੋ ਭਯੋ ਛਾਡਿ ਚਲਿਯੋ ਸੰਗ੍ਰਾਮ ॥੬॥
928.t: too kaatar aaiso bhayo chhaadd chaliyo sa(n)graam ||6||
928.e: ‘But you are so coward that you are running away from fight.’(6)
Chaupaee
‘Give me your turban and take my shalwar, the trousers. ‘When I
Wear your clothes, I will cut the enemy off’(7)
After declaring as such, she put her husband in the dungeon.
She armed herself, disguised as a man and wearing arm our she beat the war-drums.(8)
Dohira

928.g: ਸੈਨ ਸਕਲ ਲੈ ਕੈ ਚੜੀ ਸੂਰਨ ਸਕਲ ਜਤਾਇ ॥
928.t: sain sakal lai kai chaRee sooran sakal jatai ||
928.e: With the army, she raised, she displayed her power and declared,

928.g: ਬੈਰਮ ਖਾ ਮੁਹਿ ਭ੍ਰਿਤ ਕੌ ਬੀਰਾ ਦਯੋ ਬੁਲਾਇ ॥੯॥
928.t: bairam khaa muh bhirat kau beeraa dhayo bulai ||9||
928.e: ‘Bairam Khan has deputed me to fight for him.’(9)
Chaupaee
She raided through her army and rounded the enemy forces.

928.g: ਮੋ ਕਹ ਜੀਤਿ ਤਬ ਆਗੇ ਜਾਯੋ ॥੧੦॥
928.t: mo keh jeet tab aage jaayo ||10||
928.e: And (she disguised as) Bairam Khan senta massager, ‘First win me before you proceed further.’(10)

928.g: ਯੌ ਸੁਨਿ ਸੂਰ ਸਕਲ ਰਿਸ ਭਰੇ ॥
928.t: yau sun soor sakal ris bhare ||

928.e: Hearing this, all the soldiers flew into the rage,

928.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਘੇਰਿ ਦਸੌ ਦਿਸਿ ਆਏ ॥
928.t: taa ko gher dhasau dhis aae ||

928.e: And they encircled with arrows in their bows.(11)
Dohira

928.g: ਅਸਿ ਫਾਸੀ ਧਰਿ ਸਿਪਰ ਲੈ ਗੁਰਜ ਗੁਫਨ ਲੈ ਹਾਥ ॥
928.t: as faasee dhar sipar lai guraj gufan lai haath ||

928.g: ਗਿਰਿ ਗਿਰਿ ਗੇ ਜੋਧਾ ਧਰਨਿ ਬਿਧੈ ਬਰਛਿਯਨ ਸਾਥ ॥੧੨॥
928.t: gir gir ge jodhaa dharan bidhai barachhiyan saath ||12||

928.e: Bhujang Chhand

928.g: ਲਏ ਹਾਥ ਸੈਥੀ ਅਰਬ ਖਰਬ ਧਾਏ ॥
928.t: le haath saithee arab kharab dhaae ||

928.g: ਬੰਧੇ ਗੋਲ ਹਾਠੇ ਹਠੀ ਖੇਤ ਆਏ ॥
928.t: ba(n)dhe gol haaThe haThee khet aae ||
928.e: The spears in the hands, they came and rounded the enemy.

928.g: ਮਹਾ ਕੋਪ ਕੈ ਬਾਲ ਕੇ ਤੀਰ ਢੂਕੇ ॥
928.t: mahaa kop kai baal ke teer ddooke ||

928.g: ਦੁਹੂੰ ਓਰ ਤੇ ਮਾਰ ਹੀ ਮਾਰਿ ਕੂਕੇ ॥੧੩॥
928.t: dhuhoo(n) or te maar hee maar kooke ||13||
928.e: In fury they showered arrows on the lady, and the killing spread in every direction.(13)
Savaiyya

928.g: ਛੋਰਿ ਨਿਸਾਸਨ ਕੇ ਫਰਰੇ ਭਟ ਢੋਲ ਢਮਾਕਨ ਦੈ ਕਰਿ ਢੂਕੇ ॥
928.t: chhor nisaasan ke farare bhaT ddol ddamaakan dhai kar ddooke ||
928.e: Waving the flags, they followed the drum beats.

928.g: ਢਾਲਨ ਕੌ ਗਹਿ ਕੈ ਕਰ ਭੀਤਰ ਮਾਰ ਹੀ ਮਾਰਿ ਦਸੌ ਦਿਸਿ ਕੂਕੇ ॥
928.t: ddaalan kau geh kai kar bheetar maar hee maar dhasau dhis kooke ||
928.e: Bolding shields they shouted, ‘Kill them, kill them.’

928.g: ਵਾਰ ਅਪਾਰ ਬਹੇ ਕਈ ਬਾਰ ਗਏ ਛੁਟਿ ਕੰਚਨ ਕੋਟਿ ਕਨੂਕੇ ॥
928.t: vaar apaar bahe kiee baar ge chhuT ka(n)chan koT kanooke ||
928.e: Raids after raids, produced fire sparks,

928.g: ਲੋਹ ਲੁਹਾਰ ਗੜੈ ਜਨੁ ਜਾਰਿ ਉਠੈ ਇਕ ਬਾਰਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਨਾਰਿ ਭਭੂਕੇ ॥੧੪॥
928.t: loh luhaar gaRai jan jaar uThai ik baar tiranaar bhabhooke ||14||
928.e: Like the ones produced at the battering (of hot iron) at the ironsmith.(14)
Bhujang Chhand

929.e: Guiyes, Muhamadees, Dyojis and Afreedis came forward with extreme fury.

929.g: ਹਠੇ ਸੂਰ ਲੋਦੀ ਮਹਾ ਕੋਪ ਕੈ ਕੈ ॥
929.t: haThe soor lodhee mahaa kop kai kai ||

929.g: ਪਰੇ ਆਨਿ ਕੈ ਬਾਢਵਾਰੀਨ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥੧੫॥
929.t: pare aan kai baaddavaareen lai kai ||15||
929.e: Brave Lodhis were awfully enraged and fell upon, brandishing their swords.(15)
Chaupaee

929.g: ਮਹਾ ਮਾਰਿ ਬਾਨਨ ਕੀ ਗਾੜ ਐਸੀ ॥
929.t: mahaa maar baanan kee gaaR aaisee ||

929.g: ਮਨੌ ਕੁਆਰ ਕੇ ਮੇਘ ਕੀ ਬ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਜੈਸੀ ॥੧੬॥
929.t: manau kuaar ke megh kee birasaT jaisee ||16||

929.g: ਪਰੇ ਆਨਿ ਜੋਧਾ ਚਹੂੰ ਓਰ ਭਾਰੇ ॥
929.t: pare aan jodhaa chahoo(n) or bhaare ||

929.g: ਮਹਾ ਮਾਰ ਹੀ ਮਾਰਿ ਐਸੇ ਪੁਕਾਰੇ ॥
929.t: mahaa maar hee maar aaise pukaare ||

929.g: ਹਟੇ ਨਾਹਿ ਛਤ੍ਰੀ ਛਕੇ ਛੋਭ ਐਸੇ ॥
929.t: haTe naeh chhatree chhake chhobh aaise ||

929.g: ਮਨੋ ਸਾਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਕਾਲ ਕੀ ਜ੍ਵਾਲ ਜੈਸੇ ॥੧੭॥
929.t: mano saach sree kaal kee javaiaal jaise ||17||

929.g: ਧਏ ਅਰਬ ਆਛੇ ਮਹਾ ਸੂਰ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
929.t: dhe arab aachhe mahaa soor bhaaree ||

929.g: ਕਰੈ ਤੀਨਹੂੰ ਲੋਕ ਜਿਨ ਕੌ ਜੁਹਾਰੀ ॥
929.t: karai teenahoo(n) lok jin kau juhaaree ||
929.e: The great Arabian soldiers, who had commendation in all the three domains, came forward’.

929.g: ਮਨੋ ਮੇਘ ਮੈ ਦਾਮਨੀ ਦਮਕਿ ਜਾਵੈ ॥੧੮॥
929.t: mano megh mai dhaamanee dhamak jaavai ||18||
929.e: They wielded their sp’ears like the lightning in the clouds.(18)
Chaupaee
When the lady faced them, she used different types of weapons.
She would cut their faces, arms and legs,

929.g: ਪਠੈ ਧਾਮ ਜਮ ਕੇ ਸੋ ਦੀਨੇ ॥੨੦॥
929.t: paThai dhaam jam ke so dheene ||20||
929.e: And send them straight to the domain of death.(20)

929.g: ਹੈ ਗੈ ਰਥੀ ਬਿਨਾ ਅਸਿ ਭਏ ॥
929.t: hai gai rathee binaa as bhe ||
929.e: Numerous braves lost their lives and were made to relinquish their chariots, horses and elephants.
A great number lost their lives and the egoist (alive) ories commenced dancing.(21)

929.g: ਲਗੇ ਬ੍ਰਿਣਨ ਕੇ ਸੂਰਮਾ ਪਰੇ ਧਰਨਿ ਪੈ ਆਇ ॥
929.t: lage biranan ke sooramaa pare dharan pai aai ||

929.g: ਗਿਰ ਪਰੇ ਉਠਿ ਪੁਨਿ ਲਰੇ ਅਧਿਕ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਕਰਿ ਚਾਇ ॥੨੨॥
929.t: gir pare uTh pun lare adhik hiradhai kar chai ||22||

929.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਪਰਘ ਫਾਸੀ ਲਏ ਹਾਥ ਡੋਲੈ ॥
929.t: kite paragh faasee le haath ddolai ||

929.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਮਾਰ ਹੀ ਮਾਰਿ ਕੈ ਬੀਰ ਬੋਲੈ ॥੨੩॥
929.t: kite maar hee maar kai beer bolai ||23||

929.e: Dohira

929.g: ਅਤਿ ਚਿਤ ਕੋਪ ਬਢਾਇ ਕੈ ਸੂਰਨ ਸਕਲਨ ਘਾਇ ॥
929.t: at chit kop baddai kai sooran sakalan ghai ||
929.e: With extreme acrimony in their minds and after killing many fearless ones,

929.g: ਜਹਾ ਬਾਲਿ ਠਾਢੀ ਹੁਤੀ ਤਹਾ ਪਰਤ ਭੇ ਆਇ ॥੨੪॥
929.t: jahaa baal Thaaddee hutee tahaa parat bhe aai ||24||
929.e: They (enemy) reached there, where the woman was standing.(24)
Chaupaee
The enraged gallant ones came ahead but were cut instantly.
They relinquished their souls and were taken away by the fairies in the palanquins (of death).(25)
Dohira

929.g: ਜੇ ਭਟ ਆਨਿ ਅਪਛਰਨਿ ਲਏ ਬਿਵਾਨ ਚੜਾਇ ॥
929.t: je bhaT aan apachharan le bivaan chaRai ||
929.e: When the enemies were cut and taken away, the woman girded up her lions.

929.g: ਤਿਨਿ ਪ੍ਰਤਿ ਔਰ ਨਿਹਾਰਿ ਕੈ ਲਰਤੁ ਸੂਰ ਸਮੁਹਾਇ ॥੨੬॥
929.t: tin prat aauar nihaar kai larat soor samuhai ||26||
929.e: With single stroke she annihilated many enemies.

930.g: ਲਗੇ ਘਾਇ ਜੋਧਾ ਗਿਰੇ ਭੂਮਿ ਭਾਰੇ ॥
930.t: lage ghai jodhaa gire bhoom bhaare ||

930.g: ਪਰੀ ਬਾਨ ਗੋਲਾਨ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
930.t: paree baan golaan kee bheer bhaaree ||

930.g: ਬਧੇ ਗੋਲ ਗਾੜੇ ਚਲੇ ਖੇਤ ਆਏ ॥੨੮॥
930.t: badhe gol gaaRe chale khet aae ||28||

930.g: ਬਲੀ ਸੂਰ ਨ੍ਰਯਾਜੀ ਐਸੀ ਭਾਤਿ ਕੂਟੇ ॥
930.t: balee soor nrayaajee aaisee bhaat kooTe ||

930.g: ਚਲੇ ਭਾਜ ਜੋਧਾ ਸਭੈ ਸੀਸ ਫੂਟੇ ॥੨੯॥
930.t: chale bhaaj jodhaa sabhai sees fooTe ||29||

930.g: ਸੂਰ ਗਏ ਕਟਿ ਕੈ ਝਟ ਦੈ ਤਬ ਬਾਲ ਕੁਪੀ ਹਥਿਆਰ ਸੰਭਾਰੇ ॥
930.t: soor ge kaT kai jhaT dhai tab baal kupee hathiaar sa(n)bhaare ||

930.g: ਪਟਿਸ ਲੋਹ ਹਥੀ ਪਰਸੇ ਇਕ ਬਾਰ ਹੀ ਬੈਰਨਿ ਕੇ ਤਨ ਝਾਰੇ ॥
930.t: paTis loh hathee parase ik baar hee bairan ke tan jhaare ||
930.e: Some had tried to fight, some died of dread and those who were saved were as good as dead.

930.g: ਏਕ ਲਰੇ ਇਕ ਹਾਰਿ ਟਰੇ ਇਕ ਦੇਖਿ ਡਰੇ ਮਰਿ ਗੇ ਬਿਨੁ ਮਾਰੇ ॥
930.t: ek lare ik haar Tare ik dhekh ddare mar ge bin maare ||

930.g: ਬੀਰ ਕਰੋਰਿ ਸਰਾਸਨ ਛੋਰਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਣਾਨ ਕੌ ਤੋਰਿ ਸੁ ਆਨਨ ਡਾਰੇ ॥੩੦॥
930.t: beer karor saraasan chhor tiranaan kau tor su aanan ddaare ||30||
930.e: And thousands threw their bows and accepted defeat.(30)

930.g: ਟੂਟੇ ਚਹੂੰ ਓਰ ਰਿਸਿ ਕੈ ਕੈ ॥
930.t: TooTe chahoo(n) or ris kai kai ||

930.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਕੇ ਆਯੁਧੁ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥੩੧॥
930.t: bhaat bhaat ke aayudh lai kai ||31||

930.g: ਬਜ੍ਰਬਾਨ ਬਿਛੂਆ ਬਿਸਿਖ ਬਰਸਿਯੋ ਸਾਰ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
930.t: bajrabaan bichhooaa bisikh barasiyo saar apaar ||

930.g: ਊਚ ਨੀਚ ਕਾਯਰ ਸੁਭਟ ਸਭ ਕੀਨੇ ਇਕ ਸਾਰ ॥੩੨॥
930.t: uooch neech kaayar subhaT sabh keene ik saar ||32||

930.e: When such a situation arose, Arth Rai (the enemy) said aloud,

930.g: ਯਾ ਕੋ ਜਿਯਤ ਜਾਨ ਨਹੀ ਦੀਜੈ ॥
930.t: yaa ko jiyat jaan nahee dheejai ||

930.g: ਘੇਰਿ ਦਸੋ ਦਿਸਿ ਤੇ ਬਧੁ ਕੀਜੈ ॥੩੩॥
930.t: gher dhaso dhis te badh keejai ||33||
930.e: ‘Don’t let them go, surround them and give tough fight.’(33)
Listening to his spirited talk, his egoist ones got ready.
They shot the arrows from their bows and hit through the lady.(34)

930.g: ਬੇਧਿ ਬਾਨ ਜਬ ਤਨ ਗਏ ਤਬ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕੋਪ ਬਢਾਇ ॥
930.t: bedh baan jab tan ge tab tiray kop baddai ||
930.e: When her body was struck with arrows, she became wrathful.

930.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਜੁਧ ਤਿਹ ਠਾ ਕਿਯੋ ਸੋ ਮੈ ਕਹਤ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੩੫॥
930.t: amit judh teh Thaa kiyo so mai kahat banai ||35||
930.e: The frightful fighting, which she ensued, I am, now, going to relate that,(35)
The arrows, which had pierced through, she plucked them

930.g: ਜਿਨ ਕੀ ਦੇਹ ਘਾਵ ਦਿੜ ਲਾਗੇ ॥
930.t: jin kee dheh ghaav dhiR laage ||

930.e: Out, and threw the same back on the enemy.(36)
Whom so ever those arrows hit, they were taken away by the fairies

930.g: ਤੁਮਲ ਜੁਧ ਤਿਹ ਠਾ ਅਤਿ ਮਚਿਯੋ ॥
930.t: tumal judh teh Thaa at machiyo ||

930.e: Of death and none was spared the life.(37)

931.e: Arth Rai, then, came forward and embarked on a fight with her.
The woman shot four arrow and killed four of his horses.(38)
Then she cut off the chariots and killed the chariot-driver.

931.g: ਮੋਹਿਤ ਕੈ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਗਹਿ ਲੀਨੋ ॥
931.t: mohit kai taa ko geh leeno ||

931.e: She made him (Arth Rai) unconscious and beat the victory drum.(39)

931.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਬਾਧਿ ਧਾਮ ਲੈ ਆਈ ॥
931.t: taa ko baadh dhaam lai aaiee ||

931.e: She tied him and brought him home and distributed lot of wealth.

931.g: ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਕੇ ਲੋਕ ਸਕਲ ਭੇ ਰਾਜੀ ॥੪੦॥
931.t: gireh ke lok sakal bhe raajee ||40||
931.e: The victory drum were continuously beaten at her door steps and the people felt exhilarations.(40)
Dohira

931.g: ਕਾਢਿ ਭੋਹਰਾ ਤੇ ਪਤਿਹਿ ਦੀਨੋ ਸਤ੍ਰੁ ਦਿਖਾਇ ॥
931.t: kaadd bhoharaa te pateh dheeno satr dhikhai ||
931.e: She brought her husband out of the dungeon and revealed to him.

931.g: ਬਿਦਾ ਕਿਯੋ ਇਕ ਅਸ੍ਵ ਦੈ ਔ ਪਗਿਯਾ ਬਧਵਾਇ ॥੪੧॥
931.t: bidhaa kiyo ik asavai dhai aau pagiyaa badhavai ||41||
931.e: She handed over the turban and the horse and bade him goodbye.(41)(1)

931.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਛਯਾਨਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੯੬॥੧੭੨੪॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
931.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitre ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe chhayaanavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||96||1724||afajoo(n)||
931.e: Ninety-sixth Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (96)(1724)
Dohira

931.g: ਸਯਾਲਕੋਟ ਕੇ ਦੇਸ ਮੈ ਸਾਲਬਾਹਨਾ ਰਾਵ ॥
931.t: sayaalakoT ke dhes mai saalabaahanaa raav ||
931.e: In the country of Sialkote, there used to live a Raja called Salwan.

931.g: ਖਟ ਦਰਸਨ ਕੌ ਮਾਨਈ ਰਾਖਤ ਸਭ ਕੋ ਭਾਵ ॥੧॥
931.t: khaT dharasan kau maaniee raakhat sabh ko bhaav ||1||
931.e: He believed in six Shastras and loved every body.(1)

931.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਰਾਰਿ ਮਤੀ ਹੁਤੀ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਤ੍ਰਿਯ ਕੌ ਨਾਮ ॥
931.t: sree tiraparaar matee hutee taa kee tiray kau naam ||
931.e: Tripari was his wife, who worshipped goddess Bhawani during all

931.g: ਭਜੈ ਭਵਾਨੀ ਕੌ ਸਦਾ ਨਿਸੁ ਦਿਨ ਆਠੌ ਜਾਮ ॥੨॥
931.t: bhajai bhavaanee kau sadhaa nis dhin aaThau jaam ||2||
931.e: The eight watches of the day.(2)
Chaupaee

931.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਸੈਨ ਲੈ ਕੈ ਚੜਿ ਧਾਯੋ ॥
931.t: amit sain lai kai chaR dhaayo ||
931.e: When (Raja) Bikrim learnt about them, he raided with great army.
Salwan was not afraid and taking his brave ones faced the enemy.(3)
Dohira

931.g: ਤਬ ਤਾ ਸੌ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚੰਡਿਕਾ ਐਸੇ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
931.t: tab taa sau sree cha(n)ddikaa aaise kahiyo banai ||
931.e: Then the goddess Chandika told the Raja,

931.g: ਸੈਨ ਮ੍ਰਿਤਕਾ ਕੀ ਰਚੋ ਤੁਮ ਮੈ ਦੇਉ ਜਿਯਾਇ ॥੪॥
931.t: sain mritakaa kee racho tum mai dheau jiyai ||4||
931.e: ‘You prepare an army of earthen statues, and I will put life in them.’(4)
Chaupaee

931.g: ਜੋ ਜਗ ਮਾਤ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਸੋ ਕੀਨੋ ॥
931.t: jo jag maat kahiyo so keeno ||

931.e: He acted the way Universal Mother dictated and prepared an earthen army.
With the benevolence of Chandika, all those got up, laced with the weapons.(5)
Dohira

931.g: ਮਾਟੀ ਤੇ ਮਰਦ ਊਪਜੇ ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਕ੍ਰੁਧ ਬਿਸੇਖ ॥
931.t: maaTee te maradh uoopaje kar kai krudh bisekh ||
931.e: The soldiers, from the earthen shapes awoke in great fury.

931.g: ਹੈ ਗੈ ਰਥ ਪੈਦਲ ਘਨੇ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਉਠਿ ਚਲੇ ਅਨੇਕ ॥੬॥
931.t: hai gai rath paidhal ghane nirap uTh chale anek ||6||
931.e: Some became foot-soldiers, and some took Raja’s horses, elephants and chariots.( 6)
Chaupaee
The trumpets blew in the town as the intrepid roared.

931.g: ਟੂਕ ਟੂਕ ਭਾਖੈ ਜੋ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਹੈ ॥
931.t: Took Took bhaakhai jo havai hai ||

931.g: ਬਹੁਰੋ ਫੇਰਿ ਧਾਮ ਨਹਿ ਜੈ ਹੈ ॥੭॥
931.t: bahuro fer dhaam neh jai hai ||7||
931.e: And they shouted out their determination not to retreat.(7)
Dohira

931.g: ਯਹੈ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਕਰਿ ਸੂਰਮਾ ਪਰੇ ਸੈਨ ਮੈ ਆਇ ॥
931.t: yahai ma(n)tr kar sooramaa pare sain mai aai ||
931.e: With this determination they raided the (enemy) army,

931.g: ਜੋ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਕੋ ਦਲੁ ਹੁਤੋ ਸੋ ਲੈ ਚਲੇ ਉਠਾਇ ॥੮॥
931.t: jo bikram ko dhal huto so lai chale uThai ||8||
931.e: And they shook the forces of Bikrim.(8)
Bhujang Chhand

931.g: ਰਥੀ ਕੋਟਿ ਕੂਟੇ ਕਰੀ ਕ੍ਰੋਰਿ ਮਾਰੇ ॥
931.t: rathee koT kooTe karee kror maare ||

931.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਸਾਜ ਔ ਰਾਜ ਬਾਜੀ ਬਿਦਾਰੇ ॥
931.t: kite saaj aau raaj baajee bidhaare ||

931.g: ਘਨੇ ਘੂਮਿ ਜੋਧਾ ਤਿਸੀ ਭੂਮਿ ਜੂਝੇ ॥
931.t: ghane ghoom jodhaa tisee bhoom joojhe ||

932.g: ਕਹਾ ਲੌ ਗਨੌ ਮੈ ਨਹੀ ਜਾਤ ਬੂਝੇ ॥੯॥
932.t: kahaa lau ganau mai nahee jaat boojhe ||9||

932.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਸੈਨਾ ਲੈ ਚਲਿਯੋ ਤਹ ਆਪੁ ਰਾਜਾ ਸੰਗ ॥
932.t: amit sainaa lai chaliyo teh aap raajaa sa(n)g ||

932.g: ਜੋਰਿ ਕੋਰਿ ਸੁ ਬੀਰ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰਿ ਸੁਰੰਗਿ ॥
932.t: jor kor su beer ma(n)tree sasatr dhaar sura(n)g ||

932.g: ਸੂਲ ਸੈਥਿਨ ਕੇ ਲਗੇ ਅਰੁ ਬੇਧਿ ਬਾਨਨ ਸਾਥ ॥
932.t: sool saithin ke lage ar bedh baanan saath ||

932.g: ਜੂਝਿ ਜੂਝਿ ਗਏ ਤਹਾ ਰਨ ਭੂਮਿ ਮਧਿ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਥ ॥੧੦॥
932.t: joojh joojh ge tahaa ran bhoom madh pramaath ||10||

932.g: ਜਗੇ ਜੰਗ ਜੋਧਾ ਗਏ ਜੂਝਿ ਭਾਰੇ ॥
932.t: jage ja(n)g jodhaa ge joojh bhaare ||

932.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਭੂਮਿ ਘੂਮੈ ਸੁ ਮਨੋ ਮਤਵਾਰੇ ॥
932.t: kite bhoom ghoomai su mano matavaare ||
932.e: In the heavy fighting they moved like adherents

932.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਮਾਰ ਹੀ ਮਾਰਿ ਐਸੇ ਪੁਕਾਰੈ ॥
932.t: kite maar hee maar aaise pukaarai ||

932.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਛੋਰੈ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਭੇਖ ਧਾਰੈ ॥੧੧॥
932.t: kite sasatr chhorai tirayaa bhekh dhaarai ||11||
932.e: At some places they were inflicted death and at some they relaxed like women.(11)

932.g: ਜਬੈ ਆਨਿ ਜੋਧਾ ਚਹੂੰ ਘਾਤ ਗਜੇ ॥
932.t: jabai aan jodhaa chahoo(n) ghaat gaje ||

932.g: ਮਹਾ ਸੰਖ ਔ ਦੁੰਦਭੀ ਨਾਦ ਵਜੇ ॥
932.t: mahaa sa(n)kh aau dhu(n)dhabhee naadh vaje ||
932.e: When the braves from both the sides bellowed, the trumpets and conch-shells started to blow.

932.g: ਪਰੀ ਜੌ ਅਭੀਤਾਨ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
932.t: paree jau abheetaan kee bheer bhaaree ||

932.e: When the crowds of the fighters amalgamated, the goddess came in shrieking.(12) shrieking.(12)

932.g: ਤਹਾ ਆਪੁ ਲੈ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਡੌਰੂ ਬਜਾਯੋ ॥
932.t: tahaa aap lai rudhr ddauaroo bajaayo ||

932.g: ਚਤਰ ਸਾਠਿ ਮਿਲਿ ਜੋਗਨੀ ਗੀਤ ਗਾਯੋ ॥
932.t: chatar saaTh mil joganee geet gaayo ||
932.e: Shiva beat his drum too and all the sixty-four female yogis, began their singing.

932.g: ਕਹੂੰ ਕੋਪਿ ਕੈ ਡਾਕਨੀ ਹਾਕ ਮਾਰੈ ॥
932.t: kahoo(n) kop kai ddaakanee haak maarai ||

932.g: ਕਹੂੰ ਭੂਤ ਔ ਪ੍ਰੇਤ ਨਾਗੇ ਬਿਹਾਰੈ ॥੧੩॥
932.t: kahoo(n) bhoot aau pret naage bihaarai ||13||
932.e: The witches honked here and the ghosts performed naked dances.(13)
Bikrim flew into the rage, and called every body in.
With great determination they gathered there,(14)
Many bravt ones marched forward to sacrifice their lives.
Under recitation ofthe songs of death, the fighting was enhanced.(15)

932.g: ਜੇ ਚਲਿ ਦਲ ਰਨ ਮੰਡਲ ਆਏ ॥
932.t: je chal dhal ran ma(n)ddal aae ||

932.g: ਲਰਿ ਮਰਿ ਕੈ ਸਭ ਸ੍ਵਰਗ ਸਿਧਾਏ ॥੧੬॥
932.t: lar mar kai sabh savairag sidhaae ||16||

932.g: ਤਬ ਹਠਿ ਰਾਵ ਆਪਿ ਦੋਊ ਧਾਏ ॥
932.t: tab haTh raav aap dhouoo dhaae ||

932.e: Any action Bikrim took, Shri Chandika came and negated it.

932.g: ਤਿਹ ਬ੍ਰਿਣ ਏਕ ਲਗਨ ਨਹਿ ਦੇਵੈ ॥
932.t: teh biran ek lagan neh dhevai ||

932.e: She would let him hit and, considering him (Raja Salwan) as her devotee, always saved him.(19)

932.g: ਦੇਵੀ ਭਗਤ ਪਛਾਨਿ ਤਿਹ ਲਗਨ ਨ ਦੀਨੇ ਘਾਇ ॥
932.t: dhevee bhagat pachhaan teh lagan na dheene ghai ||
932.e: Expecting him as the zealot ofthe goddess, she did not let him get hurt,

932.g: ਬਜ੍ਰ ਬਾਨ ਬਰਛੀਨ ਕੋ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਚਲਾਇ ॥੨੦॥
932.t: bajr baan barachheen ko bikram rahiyo chalai ||20||
932.e: In spite of god Brij Bhan’s spears and the arrows thrown by Bikrim.(20)

933.e: Chaupaee
Salwan’s principal Rani was dreaded markedly.
She used to pray to the goddess Gorja, appraising her as her future saviour.(21)
Gorja appeared and the Rani came forward and paid her obeisance.
She performed various penances and begged for her victory.(22)
Dohira

933.g: ਸਾਲਬਾਹਨ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਭਏ ਬਾਜਿਯੋ ਲੋਹ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
933.t: saalabaahan bikram bhe baajiyo loh apaar ||
933.e: Salwan and Bikrim entered the combat,

933.g: ਆਠ ਜਾਮ ਆਹਵ ਬਿਖੈ ਜੁਧ ਭਯੋ ਬਿਕਰਾਰ ॥੨੩॥
933.t: aaTh jaam aahav bikhai judh bhayo bikaraar ||23||
933.e: And for eight hours there was horrific fighting.(23)
Chaupaee
The ruler of Sialkote became furious and, engulfed in rage, eventuated the skirmishes.

933.g: ਤਨਿ ਧਨ ਬਾਨ ਬਜ੍ਰ ਸੇ ਮਾਰੇ ॥
933.t: tan dhan baan bajr se maare ||

933.e: Stretching tightly he threw Braj arrows, which made Raja Bikrim to head for the domain of death.(24)
Dohira

933.g: ਜੀਤਿ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮਾਜੀਤ ਕੋ ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਹਰਖ ਬਢਾਇ ॥
933.t: jeet bikramaajeet ko chit mai harakh baddai ||
933.e: By winning over Bikrimajeet he felt relieved.

933.g: ਅੰਤਹ ਪੁਰ ਆਵਤ ਭਯੋ ਅਧਿਕ ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇ ॥੨੫॥
933.t: a(n)teh pur aavat bhayo adhik hiradhai sukh pai ||25||
933.e: And, at last, he felt blissful.(25)
Chaupaee

933.g: ਸੁਨ੍ਯੋ ਜੁ ਬਰੁ ਰਾਨੀ ਜੂ ਪਾਯੋ ॥
933.t: sunayo ju bar raanee joo paayo ||
933.e: When the Raja returned, he came to know the boon, which the Rani had been granted.

933.g: ਮੋ ਕੌ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਜੀਤਿ ਇਹ ਦਈ ॥
933.t: mo kau kahiyo jeet ieh dhiee ||

933.g: ਤਾ ਸੌ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਅਧਿਕ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਗਈ ॥੨੬॥
933.t: taa sau preet adhik havai giee ||26||
933.e: He thought, ‘she has made the victory possible, therefore, I must love her more.’(26)

933.g: ਹਮਰੇ ਹਿਤ ਇਹ ਰਾਨਿਯੈ ਲੀਨੀ ਗੌਰਿ ਮਨਾਇ ॥
933.t: hamare hit ieh raaniyai leenee gauar manai ||

933.g: ਰੀਝਿ ਭਗੌਤੀ ਬਰੁ ਦਯੋ ਤਬ ਹਮ ਜਿਤੇ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੨੭॥
933.t: reejh bhagauatee bar dhayo tab ham jite banai ||27||

933.g: ਨਿਸ ਦਿਨ ਰਹੈ ਤਵਨ ਕੇ ਡੇਰੈ ॥
933.t: nis dhin rahai tavan ke dderai ||

933.e: Every day Raja started to stay with her and abandoned going to other Ranis.
When many months have gone by the goddess granted him a son.(28)
Be was given the name of Rasaloo and the goddess Chandika willed,

933.g: ਜਾ ਸਮ ਔਰ ਨ ਜਗ ਮੈ ਕੋਈ ॥੨੯॥
933.t: jaa sam aauar na jag mai koiee ||29||
933.e: ‘Be will be a great celibate and gallant person and there will not be any like him in the world.’(29)
As he grew, he commenced going on hunting and killing many deer.
He travelled all the countries and never dreaded any body.(30)
Coming back after hunting, he would sit down to play chess.
He would win over many other Rajas and feel delighted.(31)

933.g: ਏਕ ਡੋਮ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਆਯੋ ॥
933.t: ek ddom taa ko gireh aayo ||

933.e: Once a bard came to him and started to play with Rasaloo.

934.e: Mter losing all his belongings and horses, that clever man said,(32)
‘I will accept you as a chess-master only if you do what I say.

934.g: ਤਬ ਇਹ ਖੇਲ ਜੀਤਿ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਆਵੋ ॥੩੩॥
934.t: tab ieh khel jeet gireh aavo ||33||
934.e: ‘You play the game with the killer-Raja and come back home alive.’(33)
Harking to this, Rasaloo mounted his horse started his journey.
He came to the country of killer-Raja, and started to play with that Raja.(34)

934.g: ਤਬ ਸਿਰਕਪ ਛਲ ਅਧਿਕ ਸੁ ਧਾਰੇ ॥
934.t: tab sirakap chhal adhik su dhaare ||

934.e: In spite of all his cleverness, the killer-Raja lost all his arms, clothes and belongings.
After losing all his wealth he bet his head and that too the lucky Rasaloo won over.(35)
After winning over when he was taking him to kill, he heard this from the direction of the Rani.

934.g: ਜਿਯ ਤੇ ਬਧ ਯਾ ਕੌ ਨਹਿ ਕੀਜੈ ॥੩੬॥
934.t: jiy te badh yaa kau neh keejai ||36||
934.e: ‘Let us get his daughter Kokila and do not kill him.’(36)

934.g: ਤਬ ਤਿਹ ਜਾਨ ਮਾਫ ਕੈ ਦਈ ॥
934.t: tab teh jaan maaf kai dhiee ||

934.e: Then he pardoned his life and took his daughter Kokila.

934.g: ਤਾ ਕੇ ਬੀਚ ਰਾਖ ਤਿਹ ਧਾਰਿਯੋ ॥੩੭॥
934.t: taa ke beech raakh teh dhaariyo ||37||
934.e: In the wilderness he built a house and he kept her there.(37)
Although her childhood had gone past and .the youth has taken over,

934.g: ਰਾਜਾ ਨਿਕਟ ਨ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਆਵੈ ॥
934.t: raajaa nikaT na taa ke aavai ||

934.g: ਯਾ ਤੇ ਅਤਿ ਰਾਨੀ ਦੁਖੁ ਪਾਵੇ ॥੩੮॥
934.t: yaa te at raanee dhukh paave ||38||
934.e: Raja would not come to see (that) Rani and the Rani would get very upset.(38)
One day when Raja passed by, the Rani said,

934.g: ਹਮ ਕੋ ਲੈ ਤੁਮ ਸੰਗ ਸਿਧਾਰੌ ॥
934.t: ham ko lai tum sa(n)g sidhaarau ||

934.g: ਬਨ ਮੈ ਜਹਾ ਮ੍ਰਿਗਨ ਕੌ ਮਾਰੌ ॥੩੯॥
934.t: ban mai jahaa miragan kau maarau ||39||
934.e: ‘Please take me with you to place where you go for deer hunting.’(39)

934.g: ਜਹ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਹਨਤ ਹੇਤ ਤਹ ਆਯੋ ॥
934.t: jeh mirag hanat het teh aayo ||
934.e: Raja took her with him where he was going for hunting the deer.

934.g: ਦੈ ਫੇਰਾ ਸਰ ਸੌ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
934.t: dhai feraa sar sau mirag maariyo ||

934.e: Raja killed the deer with his own arrows and she witnessed the whole scene.(40)
Then the Rani said, ‘Listen my Raja, ‘I can kill the deer with the sharp arrows of my eyes.

934.g: ਦ੍ਰਿਗ ਸਰ ਸੋ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਕੋ ਹੌ ਮਾਰੌ ॥
934.t: dhirag sar so mirag ko hau maarau ||

934.e: You stay here and watch all the episode.(41)
Unveiling her face, Kokila came forward and the deer was dazed to her.
On seeing her extreme beauty, it kept standing there and did not run away.(42)

934.g: ਕਰ ਸੌ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਰਾਨੀ ਜਬ ਗਹਿਯੋ ॥
934.t: kar sau mirag raanee jab gahiyo ||

934.e: Rasaloo saw her holding the deer with her hands and he was astonished to see this miracle.
He felt humiliated and cut the ears of the deer and made it to run away.(43)

934.g: ਕਾਨ ਕਟਿਯੋ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਲਖਿ ਜਬ ਪਾਯੋ ॥
934.t: kaan kaTiyo mirag lakh jab paayo ||

934.e: When its ears were cut off, it came running under the palace,
Where the Raja of the country of Eeswari chased him it on his horse.(44)

934.g: ਤਬ ਆਗੇ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਧਾਯੋ ॥
934.t: tab aage taa ke mirag dhaayo ||

934.g: ਹਰਿ ਅਰਿ ਸਰ ਤਾ ਕੌ ਤਨੁ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ॥੪੫॥
934.t: har ar sar taa kau tan maariyo ||45||

934.e: When he came across Kokila, he said to her,

934.g: ਜਾ ਕੋ ਭੇਦ ਨ ਪਾਵਤ ਕੋਊ ॥੪੬॥
934.t: jaa ko bhedh na paavat kouoo ||46||
934.e: ‘Let you and me stay here, so that no body could know.’(46)

934.g: ਹੈ ਤੇ ਉਤਰ ਭਵਨ ਪਗ ਧਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
934.t: hai te utar bhavan pag dhaariyo ||

934.e: Dismounting the horse he came in his palace and took Kokila with him.
After making love with her, he left the place and next day, again, he came back,(47)
Then the Mynah (bird) told, ‘Kokila why are you behaving foolishly.’

934.g: ਯੌ ਸੁਨਿ ਬੈਨ ਤਾਹਿ ਹਨਿ ਡਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
934.t: yau sun bain taeh han ddaariyo ||

934.g: ਤਬ ਸੁਕ ਤਿਹ ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਉਚਾਰਿਯੋ ॥੪੮॥
934.t: tab suk teh ieh bhaat uchaariyo ||48||
934.e: Hearing this she killed her and, then, the parrot said,(48)
‘It is good you have killed Mynah as she loved the Raja of Sindh.
‘Now you take me in your hands and don’t let me remain in the cage.’(49)
Sortha

934.g: ਜਿਨਿ ਰੀਸਾਲੂ ਧਾਇ ਇਹ ਠਾ ਪਹੁੰਚੈ ਆਇ ਕੈ ॥
934.t: jin reesaaloo dhai ieh Thaa pahu(n)chai aai kai ||
934.e: ‘Lest, Raja Rasaloo comes here,

934.g: ਮੁਹਿ ਤੁਹਿ ਸਿੰਧੁ ਬਹਾਇ ਜਮਪੁਰ ਦੇਇ ਪਠਾਇ ਲਖਿ ॥੫੦॥
934.t: muh tuh si(n)dh bahai jamapur dhei paThai lakh ||50||
934.e: ‘Throws us in (the river) Sindh and despatches us to the domain of death.’(50)

935.e: Chaupaee

935.g: ਤਬ ਤਿਹ ਕਾਢਿ ਹਾਥ ਪੈ ਲਯੋ ॥
935.t: tab teh kaadd haath pai layo ||

935.e: Then she took it (the parrot) out and sat it on her hand but, escaping her looks, it flew away,
And went to Rasaloo and told, ‘A thief had come to your house.’(51)
Learning this Rasaloo walked fast and reached the palace immediately.
When Kokila learnt this, she wrapped around (the other Raja) a mat and hid him away.(52)

935.g: ਜਨੁ ਕਰਿ ਰਾਹੁ ਲੂਟਿ ਸਸਿ ਲਯੋ ॥
935.t: jan kar raahu looT sas layo ||
935.e: ‘Why is your face getting pale, as if god Rahu has squeezed light out of Moon?
‘Where has gone the pinkish sparkle of your eyes? Why is your bedding become slack?’(53)
Dohira

935.g: ਜਬ ਤੇ ਗਏ ਅਖੇਟ ਤੁਮ ਤਬ ਤੇ ਮੈ ਦੁਖ ਪਾਇ ॥
935.t: jab te ge akheT tum tab te mai dhukh pai ||
935.e: (She replied) Since the time you went out on hunting, I have been living in adversity.

935.g: ਘਾਯਲ ਜ੍ਯੋ ਘੂੰਮਤ ਰਹੀ ਬਿਨਾ ਤਿਹਾਰੇ ਰਾਇ ॥੫੪॥
935.t: ghaayal jayo ghoo(n)mat rahee binaa tihaare rai ||54||
935.e: ‘I have been rolling around like an injured person.(54)
Chaupaee
‘Such a wind blew that slipped my mattress out and put in me an urge for love-making.
‘I whirl around like an injured baby of a deer.(55)

935.g: ਉਡਗ ਸਹਿਤ ਨਿਸਿ ਜਨੁ ਰਵਿ ਟੂਟੀ ॥
935.t: auddag sahit nis jan rav TooTee ||
935.e: ‘My pearly necklace is broken. The Moonlit night is destroyed by the Sun rays.

935.g: ਹੌ ਅਤਿ ਦਖਿਤ ਮੈਨ ਸੌ ਭਈ ॥
935.t: hau at dhakhit main sau bhiee ||

935.g: ਯਾ ਤੇ ਸੇਜ ਢੀਲ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਗਈ ॥੫੬॥
935.t: yaa te sej ddeel havai giee ||56||
935.e: ‘Without making love 1 am distressed and, consequently, my bed is slackened.(56)
Dohira

935.g: ਤਵ ਦਰਸਨ ਲਖਿ ਚਿਤ ਕੋ ਮਿਟਿ ਗਯੋ ਸੋਕ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
935.t: tav dharasan lakh chit ko miT gayo sok apaar ||
935.e: ‘Seeing you, now, all my anxiety has diminished,

935.g: ਜ੍ਯੋ ਚਕਵੀ ਪਤਿ ਆਪਨੇ ਦਿਵਕਰ ਨੈਨ ਨਿਹਾਰ ॥੫੭॥
935.t: jayo chakavee pat aapane dhivakar nain nihaar ||57||
935.e: ‘And I am beholding you the way the bird chakvi gets absorbed in the Moon.’(57)
Chaupaee
Thus Rani cajoled Raja with domestic sweet-talk,

935.g: ਪੁਨਿ ਤਾ ਸੌ ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਉਚਾਰੋ ॥
935.t: pun taa sau ieh bhaat uchaaro ||

935.e: And then said, ‘Listen to me my Raja,(58)

935.g: ਹਮ ਤੁਮ ਕਰ ਮੇਵਾ ਦੋਊ ਲੇਹੀ ॥
935.t: ham tum kar mevaa dhouoo lehee ||

935.g: ਡਾਰਿ ਡਾਰਿ ਯਾ ਸਫ ਮੈ ਦੇਹੀ ॥
935.t: ddaar ddaar yaa saf mai dhehee ||
935.e: ‘We both will eat the sultanas and then throw them towards the mat.

935.g: ਹਮ ਦੋਊ ਦਾਵ ਇਹੈ ਬਦ ਡਾਰੈ ॥
935.t: ham dhouoo dhaav ihai badh ddaarai ||

935.e: ‘We both will aim at the centre and one who hits the edge will lose.’(59)
Dohira

935.g: ਤਬ ਦੁਹੂੰਅਨ ਮੇਵਾ ਲਯੋ ਐਸੇ ਬੈਨ ਬਖਾਨਿ ॥
935.t: tab dhuhoo(n)an mevaa layo aaise bain bakhaan ||
935.e: Deciding upon this, they took sultanas.

935.g: ਚਤੁਰਿ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਅਤਿ ਚਿਤ ਹੁਤੋ ਇਹੀ ਬੀਚ ਗਯੋ ਜਾਨਿ ॥੬੦॥
935.t: chatur nirapat at chit huto ihee beech gayo jaan ||60||
935.e: Raja was very intelligent and he had envisaged the secret,(60)
Chaupaee
And he said, ‘Listen, my beloved Kokila Rani,
‘I have just defeated a deer and, dreaded, it is hiding in the bushes.’(61)
When Raja told her this, she accepted that Raja was really talking about the deer.

935.g: ਕਹੇ ਤੌ ਤੁਰਤ ਤਾਹਿ ਹਨਿ ਲ੍ਯਾਊ ॥
935.t: kahe tau turat taeh han layaauoo ||

936.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਤੁਮ ਕੋ ਮਾਸੁ ਖਵਾਊ ॥੬੨॥
936.t: taa ko tum ko maas khavaauoo ||62||
936.e: He added, ‘If you say so, I will go and kill that deer and bring its meat for your eating.’(62)

936.g: ਚਾਹਤ ਥੀ ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਸੋ ਭਈ ॥
936.t: chaahat thee chit mai so bhiee ||
936.e: Kokila was very much pleased to hear this as she already wanted this to happen.

936.g: ਯਹ ਇਨ ਮੂੜ ਭੇਦ ਨਹਿ ਪਾਯੋ ॥
936.t: yeh in mooR bhedh neh paayo ||

936.g: ਤਜਿ ਯਾ ਕੌ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਕੋ ਤਬ ਧਾਯੋ ॥੬੩॥
936.t: taj yaa kau mirag ko tab dhaayo ||63||
936.e: She could not acquiesces the real purpose and Raja went out towards the deer.(63)
With bow and arrow in his hands, Raja stood on the stairs.

936.g: ਜਬ ਹੋਡੀ ਤਿਹ ਠਾ ਚਲਿ ਆਯੋ ॥
936.t: jab hoddee teh Thaa chal aayo ||

936.e: When the deer came towards that side, Rasaloo said jovially,(64)

936.g: ਮੋ ਪਰ ਪ੍ਰਥਮ ਘਾਇ ਕਹ ਕਰੋ ॥
936.t: mo par pratham ghai keh karo ||
936.e: ‘Now 1 tell you that you must attack me with great care.’
With full control upon his arms and Rasaloo pulled hard and shot an arrow.(65)
The arrow hit him (the Raja inside the mat) and with one shot alone he was thrown on the ground.

936.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਤੁਰਤ ਮਾਸੁ ਕਟਿ ਲੀਨੋ ॥
936.t: taa ko turat maas kaT leeno ||

936.e: He cut his meat and, after roasting, gave that to Kokila.(66)
When Kokila ate that meat, she relished it tastefully and said,

936.g: ਜਾ ਕੇ ਤੁਲਿ ਮਾਸੁ ਕੋਊ ਨਾਹੀ ॥
936.t: jaa ke tul maas kouoo naahee ||

936.e: ‘There has never been the meat like this before and I feel very touch satiated.’(67)
Then Rasaloo told her, ‘This is the same deer, with whom you made

936.g: ਜਿਯਤ ਤੂ ਜਾ ਸੌ ਭੋਗ ਕਮਾਯੋ ॥
936.t: jiyat too jaa sau bhog kamaayo ||

936.e: Love and now you have eaten it.’(68)

936.g: ਜਬ ਯਹ ਤਨਿਕ ਭਨਿਕ ਸੁਨਿ ਪਈ ॥
936.t: jab yeh tanik bhanik sun piee ||

936.e: When she heard this, her rosy cheeks turned pale (and thought),
‘It is blasphemous to live in a world where my loved one is killed.’(69)
Dohira

936.g: ਸੁਨਤ ਕਟਾਰੀ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਕੀ ਲੈ ਅਪਨੇ ਉਰਿ ਮਾਰਿ ॥
936.t: sunat kaTaaree nirapat kee lai apane ur maar ||
936.e: Immediately learning about this, she pulled a dagger and thrust it into her body,

936.g: ਉਰਿ ਹਨਿ ਧੋਲਹਰ ਤੇ ਗਿਰੀ ਹੋਡਿਹਿ ਨੈਨ ਨਿਹਾਰ ॥੭੦॥
936.t: aur han dholahar te giree hoddeh nain nihaar ||70||
936.e: And, with the vision of deer in her eyes, fell down the palace.(70)

936.g: ਉਦਰ ਕਟਾਰੀ ਮਾਰਿ ਕੈ ਪਰੀ ਮਹਲ ਤੈ ਟੂਟਿ ॥
936.t: audhar kaTaaree maar kai paree mahal tai TooT ||
936.e: She had fallen over the palace after pushing the dagger through her

936.g: ਏਕ ਘਰੀ ਸਸਤਕ ਰਹੀ ਬਹੁਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਗੇ ਛੂਟਿ ॥੭੧॥
936.t: ek gharee sasatak rahee bahur praan ge chhooT ||71||
936.e: Body and ultimately lost her breath.(71)
Chaupaee

936.g: ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਤੇ ਟੂਟਿ ਧਰਨਿ ਪਰ ਪਰੀ ॥
936.t: gireh te TooT dharan par paree ||

936.g: ਜੋ ਬਨਿਤਾ ਪਤਿ ਆਪਨੋ ਤ੍ਯਾਗ ਔਰ ਪੈ ਜਾਇ ॥
936.t: jo banitaa pat aapano tayaag aauar pai jai ||
936.e: The woman, who abandons her husband and goes to others,

936.g: ਸੋ ਐਸੋ ਪੁਨਿ ਤੁਰਤ ਹੀ ਕ੍ਯੋ ਨਹਿ ਲਹਤ ਸਜਾਇ ॥੭੩॥
936.t: so aaiso pun turat hee kayo neh lahat sajai ||73||
936.e: Why shouldn’t that woman be punished immediately?(73)(1)

936.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਪਖ੍ਯਾਨੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਯਾ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਭੂਪ ਸੰਬਾਦੇ ਸਤਾਨਵੋ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੯੭॥੧੭੯੭॥ਅਫਜੂੰ॥
936.t: eit sree charitr pakhayaane tirayaa charitre ma(n)tree bhoop sa(n)baadhe sataanavo charitr samaapatam sat subham sat ||97||1797||afajoo(n)||
936.e: Ninety-seventh Parable of Auspicious Chritars Conversation of the Raja and the Minister, Completed with Benediction. (97)(1 797)
Dohira

936.g: ਚੰਦ੍ਰਭਗਾ ਸਰਿਤਾ ਨਿਕਟਿ ਰਾਝਨ ਨਾਮਾ ਜਾਟ ॥
936.t: cha(n)dhrabhagaa saritaa nikaT raajhan naamaa jaaT ||
936.e: On the banks of the river Chenab, a Jat Peasant, named Ranjha used to live.

936.g: ਜੋ ਅਬਲਾ ਨਿਰਖੈ ਤਿਸੈ ਜਾਤ ਸਦਨ ਪਰਿ ਖਾਟ ॥੧॥
936.t: jo abalaa nirakhai tisai jaat sadhan par khaaT ||1||
936.e: Any damsel who saw him, would get mad to have love bond with him.(1)
Chaupaee

937.e: His looks had luring effect like the sight of a deer for the hunter.

937.g: ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਅਧਿਕ ਰੀਝ ਕੇ ਰਹੈ ॥
937.t: chit mai adhik reejh ke rahai ||

937.e: They would yearn for him, and always recited ‘Ranjha, Ranjha.’(2)
There was time when the famine had spread over the country.

937.g: ਜਿਯਤ ਨ ਕੌ ਨਰ ਬਚਿਯੋ ਨਗਰ ਮੈ ॥
937.t: jiyat na kau nar bachiyo nagar mai ||

937.g: ਸੋ ਉਬਰਿਯੋ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਧਨੁ ਘਰ ਮੈ ॥੩॥
937.t: so ubariyo jaa ke dhan ghar mai ||3||
937.e: Lot of people did not escape death and the only ones who were wealthy survived.(3)

937.g: ਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਦੇਵਿ ਇਕ ਰਾਨਿ ਨਗਰ ਮੈ ॥
937.t: chitr dhev ik raan nagar mai ||

937.g: ਰਾਝਾ ਏਕ ਪੂਤ ਤਿਹ ਘਰ ਮੈ ॥
937.t: raajhaa ek poot teh ghar mai ||
937.e: In the city a Rani named Chitardevi, there used to live who had this son named Ranjah.

937.g: ਤਾ ਕੇ ਔਰ ਨ ਬਚਿਯੋ ਕੋਈ ॥
937.t: taa ke aauar na bachiyo koiee ||

937.e: Except those two, the mother and the son, none had survived.(4)
When the hunger tormented the woman, she thought of a plan.
She would go to other houses to grind flour, and the left-over there, she would bring home to eat.(5)

937.g: ਪੁਨਿ ਬਿਧਿ ਤਹਾ ਬ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਅਤਿ ਦਈ ॥
937.t: pun bidh tahaa birasaT at dhiee ||

937.g: ਔਰ ਲੋਗ ਸਭ ਤਹ ਕੋ ਮਰਿਯੋ ॥
937.t: aauar log sabh teh ko mariyo ||
937.e: This way she eliminated her hunger and, then, suddenly, Almighty
Had a benevolent observation; all that was dry became green(7)

937.g: ਪੂਤ ਜਾਟ ਕੋ ਸਭ ਕੋ ਜਾਨੈ ॥
937.t: poot jaaT ko sabh ko jaanai ||

937.g: ਤਿਸ ਤੇ ਕੋਊ ਨ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਪਛਾਨੈ ॥
937.t: tis te kouoo na rahiyo pachhaanai ||
937.e: All, now, realised that he (Ranjha) was the son of a Jat and no one realised his real identity (that he was the son of a Rani).
The famine subsided and the age of sensuality over powered.(8)
He used to come back in the evening after grazing the cattle and became known as Ranjah.

937.g: ਪੂਤ ਜਾਟ ਕੋ ਤਿਹ ਸਭ ਜਾਨੈ ॥
937.t: poot jaaT ko teh sabh jaanai ||

937.e: Every body thought him to be the son of a Jat and none acknowledged him as the son of a Raja.(9)

937.g: ਅਬ ਚਲਿ ਬਾਤ ਹੀਰ ਪੈ ਰਹੀ ॥
937.t: ab chal baat heer pai rahee ||
937.e: Thus far we have talked about Ranjha, now we consider Heer.

937.g: ਤੁਮ ਕੌ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਕਥਾ ਸੁਨਾਊ ॥
937.t: tum kau taa kee kathaa sunaauoo ||

937.e: I will narrate you their story to delight your mind.(10)
Arril

937.g: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਰਾਇ ਕੇ ਨਗਰ ਅਪਸਰਾ ਇਕ ਰਹੈ ॥
937.t: ei(n)dhr rai ke nagar apasaraa ik rahai ||
937.e: In the city of Inder Rai, a damsel lived,

937.g: ਮੈਨ ਕਲਾ ਤਿਹ ਨਾਮ ਸਕਲ ਜਗ ਯੌ ਕਹੈ ॥
937.t: main kalaa teh naam sakal jag yau kahai ||
937.e: Her name was known all over the world.

937.g: ਤਾ ਕੌ ਰੂਪ ਨਰੇਸ ਜੋ ਕੋਊ ਨਿਹਾਰਹੀ ॥
937.t: taa kau roop nares jo kouoo nihaarahee ||
937.e: Any Raja who saw her would be overcome with lust.

937.g: ਹੋ ਗਿਰੈ ਧਰਨਿ ਪਰ ਝੂਮਿ ਮੈਨ ਸਰ ਮਾਰਹੀ ॥੧੧॥
937.t: ho girai dharan par jhoom main sar maarahee ||11||
937.e: After reeling and spinning, they would fall flat on the ground. ||11||
Chaupaee
At that place, once the ascetic Kapil Munni had come and seen (the damsel) Maneka,

937.g: ਤਿਹ ਲਖਿ ਮੁਨਿ ਬੀਰਜ ਗਿਰਿ ਗਯੋ ॥
937.t: teh lakh mun beeraj gir gayo ||

937.g: ਚਪਿ ਚਿਤ ਮੈ ਸ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਤਿਹ ਭਯੋ ॥੧੨॥
937.t: chap chit mai sraapat teh bhayo ||12||
937.e: On her sight, his semen dripped down and he pronounced a curse,(12)

937.g: ਤੁਮ ਗਿਰਿ ਮਿਰਤ ਲੋਕ ਮੈ ਪਰੋ ॥
937.t: tum gir mirat lok mai paro ||

937.e: ‘You go to the domain of humanity and take birth into the family of Sial Jat.’

938.e: ‘You assume the name of Heer and devour the food at the household of Turks (Muslims).’(13)
Dohira

938.g: ਤਬ ਅਬਲਾ ਕੰਪਤਿ ਭਈ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਪਰਿ ਕੈ ਪਾਇ ॥
938.t: tab abalaa ka(n)pat bhiee taa ke par kai pai ||
938.e: Then the damsel, shaking, fell upon the feet of Munni and requested,

938.g: ਕ੍ਰਯੋਹੂ ਹੋਇ ਉਧਾਰ ਮਮ ਸੋ ਦਿਜ ਕਹੋ ਉਪਾਇ ॥੧੪॥
938.t: krayohoo hoi udhaar mam so dhij kaho upai ||14||
938.e: ‘Tell me some resolve so that I can escape this agony.’(14)
Chaupaee

938.g: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਸੁ ਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਮੰਡਲ ਜਬ ਜੈਹੈ ॥
938.t: ei(n)dhr su mirat ma(n)ddal jab jaihai ||

938.e: (Reply) ‘When god Indra will go to themundane world, he will call himself Ranjha.
‘He will intensively fall in love with you and will bring you back to Amrawati (domain of emancipation).(15)
Dohira

938.g: ਜੂਨਿ ਜਾਟ ਕੀ ਤਿਨ ਧਰੀ ਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਮੰਡਲ ਮੈ ਆਇ ॥
938.t: joon jaaT kee tin dharee mirat ma(n)ddal mai aai ||
938.e: She took birth in the household of a Jat.

938.g: ਚੂਚਕ ਕੇ ਉਪਜੀ ਭਵਨ ਹੀਰ ਨਾਮ ਧਰਵਾਇ ॥੧੬॥
938.t: choochak ke upajee bhavan heer naam dharavai ||16||
938.e: She appeared in the house of Choochak and called herself as Heer.(16)
Chaupaee
The time passed and the years went by,
The childhood was abandoned and the drums of the yoUth began to play.(l7)

938.g: ਤਾ ਕੋ ਹੇਰਿ ਹੀਰ ਬਲਿ ਜਾਵੈ ॥
938.t: taa ko her heer bal jaavai ||
938.e: When Ranjha would come back after grazing the cattle, Heer would go crazy,
She depicted intense love towards him and showered many affections.(18)
Dohira

938.g: ਖਾਤ ਪੀਤ ਬੈਠਤ ਉਠਤ ਸੋਵਤ ਜਾਗਤ ਨਿਤਿ ॥
938.t: khaat peet baiThat uThat sovat jaagat nit ||
938.e: Eating, drinking, sitting, standing, sleeping and awake,

938.g: ਕਬਹੂੰ ਨ ਬਿਸਰੈ ਚਿਤ ਤੇ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਦਰਸ ਨਮਿਤ ॥੧੯॥
938.t: kabahoo(n) na bisarai chit te su(n)dhar dharas namit ||19||
938.e: All the time she would not keep him out of her mind.(19)
Heer Talk

938.g: ਬਾਹਰ ਜਾਉ ਤੌ ਬਾਹਰ ਹੀ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਆਵਤ ਆਵਤ ਸੰਗ ਲਗੇਹੀ ॥
938.t: baahar jaau tau baahar hee gireh aavat aavat sa(n)g lagehee ||
938.e: ‘If he goes out, I go out too.

938.g: ਜੌ ਹਠਿ ਬੈਠਿ ਰਹੋ ਘਰ ਮੈ ਪਿਯ ਪੈਠਿ ਰਹੈ ਹਿਯ ਮੈ ਪਹਿ ਲੇਹੀ ॥
938.t: jau haTh baiTh raho ghar mai piy paiTh rahai hiy mai peh lehee ||
938.e: ‘If he stays at home I feel I am sitting with him.

938.g: ਨੀਂਦ ਹਮੈ ਨਕਵਾਨੀ ਕਰੀ ਛਿਨ ਹੀ ਛਿਨ ਰਾਮ ਸਖੀ ਸੁਪਨੇਹੀ ॥
938.t: nee(n)dh hamai nakavaanee karee chhin hee chhin raam sakhee supanehee ||
938.e: ‘He has snatched my sleep away and in the sleep he does not let me

938.g: ਜਾਗਤ ਸੋਵਤ ਰਾਤਹੂੰ ਦ੍ਯੋਸ ਕਹੂੰ ਮੁਹਿ ਰਾਝਨ ਚੈਨ ਨ ਦੇਹੀ ॥੨੦॥
938.t: jaagat sovat raatahoo(n) dhayos kahoo(n) muh raajhan chain na dhehee ||20||
938.e: Alone. ‘Day in and day out, Ranjha does not let me be in serenity.’(20)
Chaupaee
She would recite ‘Ranjhan, Ranjhan’ all the time,
